title: @origingame/engine API v1
description:
The Origin Engine API. Game code declares components and systems, and reads the world through typed views over engine memory.
Every failure is a returned Result; desc objects may omit any field; nothing reads the wall clock inside a tick.

x-og-units.cssPx: CSS pixels of the play surface, origin at the top left
x-og-units.perSecond: a rate per second: the fraction of a value that decays in one second
x-og-units.kgPerM3: kilograms per cubic metre (per square metre in the 2D profile)

x-og-modules.name: math
x-og-modules.doc: Plain math values in the three.js vocabulary. They are data: the engine owns the operations, so results are identical on every host.

x-og-modules.name: reflect
x-og-modules.doc:
Reflection: components and resources are declared once with their field layout and metadata, and registered by name.
The inspector, Tune, the probe, scene text and the wiki read this one schema. Each column factory below makes one field.

functions.name: defineComponent
functions.doc:
Declare a component: plain data stored per entity in engine memory, one column per field.
Registration is by name, so a hot reload re-registers the same component and migrates its fields by name.

params.name: name
params.doc: The component's unique name, PascalCase, as it appears in scenes and dumps.

params.name: fields
params.doc: The layout: field names to column factories, as `{ hp: f32(100) }`.

functions.returnsDoc: The token systems, queries and the world take.

functions.name: defineResource
functions.doc: Declare a resource: a reflected singleton, such as a tuning table. Its fields start at their defaults.
functions.returnsDoc: The token `world.resource` and system declarations take.

x-og-modules.name: world
x-og-modules.doc:
The world: an archetype ECS. Entities are generational handles; components are columns in engine memory.
Structural changes (spawn, despawn, insert, remove) invalidate typed views; the API refuses a stale view.

interfaces.name: World
interfaces.doc: The world a system, a command or a game callback is handed. Game code never holds a world beyond the call it was passed to.

members.name: tick
members.doc: Fixed steps taken since the world was created.

members.name: spawn
members.doc: Spawn an entity.
members.returnsDoc: The new entity, or why it was refused (a duplicate name, a dead parent).

members.name: despawn
members.doc: Despawn an entity and its descendants.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity.

members.name: alive
members.doc: Whether an entity handle is live.

members.name: has
members.doc: Whether an entity has a component.

members.name: insert
members.doc: Add a component to an entity, or overwrite it when present. A structural change.

params.name: value
params.doc: Field values; omitted fields take their defaults.

members.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity or an unregistered component.

members.name: remove
members.doc: Remove a component from an entity. A structural change.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity or a component it does not have.

members.name: get
members.doc: Copy one entity's component value. For bulk work use a system's typed views.

members.name: set
members.doc: Write some fields of one entity's component.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity or a component it does not have.

members.name: resource
members.doc: A resource's live value. Inside a system, the resource must be among the system's reads or writes (writes to set a field): an undeclared one throws in a dev or release build, naming the system and the resource, and fails the tick; a publish build refuses it and logs it once per system in the engine log.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for an unregistered resource (or, in a publish build, one the running system did not declare).

members.name: find
members.doc: The entity with a name.
members.returnsDoc: Null when no live entity has the name.

members.name: nameOf
members.doc: An entity's name.
members.returnsDoc: Null for an unnamed or dead entity.

members.name: query
members.doc: A query over the current archetypes, for commands and callbacks; systems receive theirs.

members.name: events
members.doc: The events of one type emitted during the previous tick and this one, oldest first. Inside a system the event must be among its reads or writes (undeclared: thrown, or in a publish build refused and logged once).

members.name: emit
members.doc: Emit an event; readers see it this tick and the next. Inside a system the event must be among its writes (undeclared: thrown, or in a publish build refused and logged once).

members.name: instantiate
members.doc:
Spawn a loaded scene or glTF asset into the world: a root entity from the desc, then (for a scene) every scene entity under it with its components and names, or (for a glTF) a Model on the root.
Scene entity names must be free: a name already in use refuses the whole instantiation before anything spawns.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Name, parent and transform of the root entity.

members.returnsDoc: The root entity, or why it was refused (an asset still loading, a failed asset).

interfaces.name: Query
interfaces.doc: A set of matched archetypes. Iterate archetypes, never entities one by one.

members.name: archetypes
members.doc: The matched archetypes this tick.

members.name: count
members.doc: The number of matched entities.

interfaces.name: ArchetypeView
interfaces.doc: One archetype's columns for this tick. Views are invalidated by structural changes; using a stale view throws with the tick and the system it belonged to.

members.name: count
members.doc: The number of entities in the archetype.

members.name: tick
members.doc: The tick this view belongs to.

members.name: entities
members.doc: The entities as (index, generation) pairs: entity i is at 2i and 2i + 1.

members.name: entity
members.doc: The handle of entity i.

members.name: has
members.doc: Whether the archetype carries a component.

members.name: column
members.doc:
The typed views of a component's fields: one typed array per field, `count * stride` long.
Writing requires the component among the system's writes; reading among its reads or writes.

x-og-modules.name: system
x-og-modules.doc:
Systems: functions the engine calls once per tick with their matched archetypes.
A system declares what it reads and writes; a write to an undeclared component is refused at registration with the field name.
Resources and events it reaches through the world must be declared too: in a dev or release build (og run, og test) an undeclared read or write throws with the system's name and the record and fails the tick; a publish build refuses it and logs it once per system in the engine log, and the game keeps running. og.Rng among the reads may fork (a fork reads the seed only and leaves the stream as it is); a draw moves the stream, so it needs og.Rng among the writes.

functions.name: defineSystem
functions.doc: Declare a system.

members.name: name
members.doc: The system's unique name.

members.name: reads
members.doc: What it reads.

members.name: writes
members.doc: What it writes.

callbacks.name: SystemRun
callbacks.doc: A system's body. It is called once per tick; loop over `q.archetypes()`, then over rows.

params.name: q
params.doc: The archetypes matching the declared components.

params.name: time
params.doc: The Time resource for this tick.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world, for resources, events and structural changes.

x-og-modules.name: game
x-og-modules.doc: The game entry: what the bundle's default export declares.

functions.name: game
functions.doc: Declare the game. The bundle's default export is its result.

interfaces.name: Game
interfaces.doc: A declared game, the bundle's default export.

members.name: tick
members.doc: The fixed tick rate in hertz.

members.name: systems
members.doc: The systems in declaration order.

callbacks.name: FactsFn
callbacks.doc: The game's own facts for the probe's state(): a small JSON object, computed from the world without changing it.

callbacks.name: StartFn
callbacks.doc: The game's setup: called once before the first tick, after GameDesc.scene has spawned. Spawn, insert, load and set resources here; systems then only read and write their views.

x-og-modules.name: transform
x-og-modules.doc: Transforms in the three.js vocabulary: position, quaternion and scale, composed into matrixWorld down the parent chain.

functions.name: compose
functions.doc: A matrix from position, rotation and scale, as three.js Matrix4.compose.

functions.name: decompose
functions.doc: Position, rotation and scale from a matrix, as three.js Matrix4.decompose.

functions.name: lookAt
functions.doc: The rotation that points -Z from an eye towards a target, as three.js Object3D.lookAt for cameras.

params.name: up
params.doc: The up direction; the zero vector means +Y.

functions.name: fromAxisAngle
functions.doc: A rotation about an axis, as three.js Quaternion.setFromAxisAngle.

x-og-modules.name: time
x-og-modules.doc: Simulation time. Game code never reads the wall clock; it reads Time.

functions.name: setScale
functions.doc: Set the global time scale (slow motion): physics, og.anim, flipbooks and tweens advance by dt * scale from the system after the call; systems may call it.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused outside 0..10.

functions.name: hitStop
functions.doc: Freeze scaled time for `ticks` ticks from now (this tick included): physics, og.anim, flipbooks and scaled tweens hold while input, the UI, unscaled tweens and camera shake keep moving. A longer hit stop in progress is never shortened. Typical values at 60 Hz: 2-3 ticks for a light hit, 4-6 medium, 8-12 heavy, 12-20 a finishing blow (paired with slow motion).

x-og-modules.name: rng
x-og-modules.doc:
Deterministic randomness. Every random draw comes from an Rng stream; the sequence for a seed is identical on every host and in the Web scaffold's rng.ts.
Inside a system: forking needs og.Rng among the reads (a fork is derived from the seed and the label, and leaves the main stream where it is); drawing from og.Rng itself (next, range, integer, chance) moves its state, so it needs og.Rng among the writes. A stream a fork returned is the system's own to draw from.

interfaces.name: RngStream
interfaces.doc: One generator stream, forked from the Rng resource for a subsystem that must not perturb the main sequence.

members.name: seed
members.doc: The stream's derived seed.

members.name: next
members.doc: Uniform in [0, 1).

members.name: range
members.doc: Uniform in [low, high).

members.name: integer
members.doc: A uniform integer in [low, high].

members.name: chance
members.doc: True with probability p.

members.name: fork
members.doc: A fresh stream on a seed derived from this stream's seed and a label.

params.name: label
params.doc: The subsystem's name; the same label always gives the same stream.

x-og-modules.name: input
x-og-modules.doc:
Input as the game sees it: the Input resource for polling, events for edges.
The shell collects pointer, keyboard and wheel input on the main thread; the probe and the command channel inject through the same path.
Several pointers at once (multi-touch) are og.Pointers; the first four gamepads, in the W3C standard mapping, are og.Gamepad. Both are world state, as og.Input is, so they replay.

consts.name: MAX_POINTERS
consts.doc: The most pointers og.Pointers tracks at once: ids 0 (the primary pointer) to 4.

consts.name: MAX_GAMEPADS
consts.doc: The most gamepads og.Gamepad reads: pads 0 to 3.

x-og-modules.name: camera
x-og-modules.doc:
The main camera, as a resource with three.js PerspectiveCamera and OrthographicCamera parameter names.
Camera controllers are components (OrbitCamera, FollowCamera, Follow2D) on the entity the camera orbits or follows; the systems that drive them ship in TypeScript as og.systems.cameras.

functions.name: shake
functions.doc: Add screen shake: trauma, clamped to 1, which og.Camera decays by traumaDecay. The shake grows with trauma squared, so 0.1-0.2 is a light hit, 0.25-0.4 a medium one, 0.5-0.8 an explosion or a boss slam; 1 is almost never right (nauseating). Visual only. Systems may call it; it takes effect at the engine's og.camera system this tick.

functions.name: punch
functions.doc: A zoom punch: the view narrows by `amount` (0.05 is a tap, 0.15 a slam) and springs back by Camera.punchDecay. Visual only.

params.name: amount
params.doc: The fraction to zoom in (negative zooms out), -0.9 to 4.

functions.name: kick
functions.doc: A directional nudge of the view (recoil, an impact from one side): offset by `distance` along `direction`, returning by Camera.kickDecay. Visual only.

params.name: direction
params.doc: The direction to push the view (normalised here; zero does nothing).

x-og-modules.name: render
x-og-modules.doc: What is drawn: meshes with materials. Draws are instanced by (geometry, material) automatically; there is no per-object draw call.

consts.name: MAX_LIGHTS
consts.doc: The most point and spot lights one frame draws, among those in view; past it the ones brightest at the camera are kept.

consts.name: MAX_CLUSTER_LIGHTS
consts.doc: The most point and spot lights that shade one screen cluster (a 1/16 by 1/9 tile of the view and one of 24 depth slices); past it the ones brightest at the camera are kept there.

params.name: world

x-og-modules.name: load
x-og-modules.doc:
Asset loading from cooked output: `og cook` turns assets/ into cooked/ (.ogb blobs and the manifest cooked/.cook.ogt), and the runtime reads only cooked/.
Paths are asset ids: the path under assets/ (`models/ship.glb`, `scenes/main.ogt`); an `assets/` prefix is accepted. Every blob is checked against the manifest's type, schema version and cook stamp.
The game's bundle (`cooked`) is opened before the first tick and GameDesc.scene is spawned then. Loads from an open bundle complete at once on both hosts (the web host fetches the bundle's files before the engine starts); only og.load.bundle of another bundle can be pending, and it completes at a tick boundary.

functions.doc: Open another cooked bundle (the game's own `cooked` is open before the first tick). Its loads read through it once it is ready.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.doc: The cooked directory, relative to the project (or the page), such as `dlc/cooked`.

functions.returnsDoc: The bundle's handle: pending until its manifest is read, then ready or failed.

functions.doc: What an open bundle holds.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a pending, failed or non-bundle asset.

functions.doc: The game's own bundle, opened before the first tick from `cooked/`.

params.name: world

functions.returnsDoc: Refused when cooked/ was missing or unreadable (run og cook); the reason names the path.

x-og-modules.name: physics
x-og-modules.doc:
Rigid bodies over rapier (rapier3d in the 3D profile, rapier2d in 2D, both with enhanced determinism): game code owns the components, the engine's og.physics system steps them after the game's systems and writes the dynamic bodies back.
The profile is the project's (`profile "2d"` or `"3d"` in project.ogt). In 2D, bodies move in the xy plane and rotate about z; a transform keeps its z. A collider without a RigidBody is static at its transform.
The rapier world persists between ticks and is world state: snapshots, restore and the world hash cover the whole simulation. Events sent in tick N are read in tick N + 1.

consts.name: BODY_DYNAMIC
consts.doc: RigidBody.kind: moved by the solver; its Transform and Velocity are written back every tick.

consts.name: BODY_STATIC
consts.doc: RigidBody.kind: never moves; collides with dynamic bodies.

consts.name: BODY_KINEMATIC
consts.doc: RigidBody.kind: moved by game code through its Transform; its Velocity, if any, is how fast it pushes.

consts.name: LOCK_TRANSLATION_X
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no translation along x.

consts.name: LOCK_TRANSLATION_Y
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no translation along y.

consts.name: LOCK_TRANSLATION_Z
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no translation along z.

consts.name: LOCK_ROTATION_X
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no rotation about x.

consts.name: LOCK_ROTATION_Y
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no rotation about y.

consts.name: LOCK_ROTATION_Z
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no rotation about z (the 2D profile's only rotation).

consts.name: SHAPE_BOX
consts.doc: Collider.shape: a box of `size` (both profiles).

consts.name: SHAPE_SPHERE
consts.doc: Collider.shape: a sphere of `radius` (a circle in 2D).

consts.name: SHAPE_CAPSULE
consts.doc: Collider.shape: a capsule along y of `radius`, with `height` between the cap centres (both profiles).

consts.name: SHAPE_CYLINDER

functions.name: raycast
functions.doc: The nearest collider along a ray. Inside a system it sees the colliders as they were at the start of the tick (og.physics.queries records them before the game's systems); between ticks, as the world holds them.
functions.returnsDoc: The hit, or null when nothing is hit; refused for a zero direction.

functions.name: shapeCast
functions.doc: The first collider a shape meets when swept along a direction; the same view of the colliders as raycast.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The shape, its sweep and the filter.

functions.returnsDoc: The hit, or null; refused for a zero direction or an unknown mesh.

functions.name: overlap
functions.doc: Every collider overlapping a shape, sorted by entity id; the same view of the colliders as raycast.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The shape, its placement and the filter.

functions.name: setMesh
functions.doc: Register (or replace) the geometry a convex or triangle-mesh Collider names by its mesh handle. Loaded glTF geometries are registered under their own handles already; meshes are assets, not world state.

params.name: mesh
params.doc: The handle colliders name in Collider.mesh.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an empty, non-finite or out-of-range mesh.

functions.name: ropePoints
functions.doc: An og.Rope's points after the last step, from its entity to its end (empty before its first step). The engine draws visible ropes itself; this is for game logic and custom drawing.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.Rope.

functions.name: clothPoints
functions.doc: An og.Cloth's points after the last step, row by row (`columns` per row, rows downwards from the top edge).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.Cloth.

functions.name: fluidParticles
functions.doc: An og.Fluid2D's particle positions after the last step, in world space.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.Fluid2D.

functions.name: fluid3dParticles
functions.doc: An og.Fluid3D's particle positions after the last step, in world space (emitted particles last, in the order they appeared).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.Fluid3D.

functions.name: waterHeight
functions.doc: The surface height of an og.WaterSurface (world y) or an og.WaterLine (world y at `x`; `z` ignored) at a point, as the last step left it: for boats that bob and spray that starts on the surface.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without water; outside the water, its rest level.

functions.name: vehicleWheels
functions.doc: An og.Vehicle's wheels after the last step (front left, front right, rear left, rear right), for drawing wheel models.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without a vehicle.

functions.name: ragdollRigFromSkeleton
functions.doc: A ragdoll rig from a loaded skeleton (og.load.animation's `skeleton`): a bone per joint of its first skin, parents first, each from its joint's rest pose to its first child joint, every bone naming its joint and the rig naming the skeleton. Pass it to og.physics.setRagdollRig, edited or not.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a skeleton that is not loaded or has no skin.

functions.name: setRagdollRig
functions.doc: Give an entity with an og.Ragdoll its bones (and, from og.physics.ragdollRigFromSkeleton, the skeleton they stand for: its og.Model is then drawn blended from the animation towards the bones by og.Ragdoll.blend). While weight is 0 the bones follow the rig's rest pose at the entity. Rigs are assets, not world state: kept by the engine and given again to a reloaded world.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an empty rig or a parent that does not come before its child.

functions.name: ragdollPose
functions.doc: An og.Ragdoll's bones after the last step, in rig order (empty before its first step).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without a ragdoll.

x-og-modules.name: atmosphere
x-og-modules.doc:
Fog, a procedural sky, the day-night cycle, weather and water, declared as resources and components (the E5 round). Everything is off by default: a world that sets none of them draws exactly as before.
The day-night clock is a function of the tick (DayNight.start plus the simulated time times speed), so it is the same on every run and after a restore; rendering reads the world and never writes it.

consts.name: WEATHER_NONE
consts.doc: Weather.kind: clear.

consts.name: WEATHER_RAIN
consts.doc: Weather.kind: rain streaks falling with the wind, the light dimmed and a grey distance fog.

consts.name: WEATHER_SNOW
consts.doc: Weather.kind: flakes drifting down on gusts, a pale fog.

consts.name: WEATHER_DUST
consts.doc: Weather.kind: dust blowing along the wind near the ground, a warm thick fog.

consts.name: WEATHER_MIST
consts.doc: Weather.kind: no particles, a dense low height fog.

functions.name: timeOfDay
functions.doc: The DayNight clock at the current tick, in hours from 0 to 24 (its start when the cycle is off): for lamps that light at dusk and shops that close at night. Inside a system, declare og.DayNight among its reads.

x-og-modules.name: anim
x-og-modules.doc:
Skeletal animation over og-anim: glTF skins and clips (cooked into the `<model>#anim` blob, loaded with og.load.animation), blend-tree graphs with layered state machines, root motion, two-bone and FABRIK IK and blendshapes, evaluated by the engine's og.anim system after the game's systems and before physics.
Game code owns the components and sets players, graph parameters and IK targets; og.anim writes the pose (kept as world state in the `og.anim` state block, so snapshots, restore and the world hash cover it), the joint palette, root motion into og.Transform and the fields marked written. Asset handles are what og.load.animation and og.anim.graph answer; 0 is none.
Clips bind to a skeleton's nodes by name, so a clip of one rig plays on another with the same node names; a rig with other names or proportions plays it retargeted (og.anim.retarget at run time, or a model's `animation { library }` import setting at cook time). Assets are not world state: a hot reload registers them again.

functions.name: graph
functions.doc: Register a blend-tree graph for AnimationGraph.asset. Its `clip` lines are resolved by name against `clips`.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation owns the graph.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The text and the clips it may name.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a parse error (the reason names the line), a clip name `clips` lacks, or an invalid graph.

functions.name: humanoid
functions.doc: The standard humanoid bones of a skeleton, as retargeting sees them: to check a rig before retargeting onto it.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation owns the skeleton.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unregistered skeleton or rig, or a rig naming a node the skeleton lacks.

functions.name: retarget
functions.doc: A new clip for `target` from a clip of `source`: each animated humanoid bone turns as the source's does from its rest pose (after a rest correction, so a T-pose drives an A-pose and other bone frames agree), the target keeps its bone lengths, the hips travel the source's distance scaled by the leg ratio (root motion kept, hip height scaled), and with footIk the feet land where the source's do, scaled. Same name, duration and markers. The cook does the same for a model's `animation { library }` import setting; this is for clips chosen at run time.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation owns the skeletons and the clip.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The clip, the two skeletons and their rigs.

functions.returnsDoc: The new clip (what AnimationPlayer.clip takes). Refused for an unregistered clip, skeleton or rig, a skeleton without recognisable hips (name them in a `type rig` file), or a rig naming a missing node.

functions.name: clip
functions.doc: The index of a flipbook clip by name, for Flipbook.clip: `og.anim.clip(hero, "walk_down")`. -1 when the sheet has no such clip.

x-og-modules.name: tween
x-og-modules.doc:
Tweens: animate any numeric field of a component (og.Transform.position, og.Sprite.color, og.Sprite.opacity, a game's own f32) from its value to a target over time with an easing curve, a delay, loops and yoyo; chain them in sequences or run them in parallel. Advanced by the engine's og.tween system after the game's systems and before og.anim and physics, by scaled time (slow motion, hit stop) unless unscaled.
Running tweens are world state (the og.tween state block): snapshots, restore and the world hash cover them. og.TweenCompleted reports a tween or group that ends on its own; a cancelled one, or one whose entity or component went away, ends silently.
Feel presets are tweens too: og.tween.squash (squash and stretch that recovers) and og.tween.flash (a hit flash that fades).

functions.name: to
functions.doc: Start a tween. Systems may call it; it first moves in this tick's og.tween run.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The field, the values and the timing.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity, a component it lacks, a field that is not numeric, or values of the wrong length.

functions.name: sequence
functions.doc: Start tweens one after another (each with its own delay, duration and loops); the time one leaves over goes to the next.

functions.name: parallel
functions.doc: Start tweens together; the group ends with the last one.

functions.name: cancel
functions.doc: Stop a tween where it is (no event).
functions.returnsDoc: False when it was not running.

functions.name: cancelEntity
functions.doc: Stop every tween of an entity (no events), say before starting a new reaction.
functions.returnsDoc: How many stopped.

functions.name: active
functions.doc: Whether a tween is still running.

functions.name: squash
functions.doc: Squash and stretch the entity's og.Transform.scale (cancels its earlier squash).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without og.Transform.

functions.name: flash
functions.doc: Flash the entity's og.Sprite, or its og.Mesh (cancels its earlier flash).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity with neither og.Sprite nor og.Mesh.

x-og-modules.name: tilemap
x-og-modules.doc:
Tilemaps: layers of tiles from a tileset atlas (an `.ogt` of `type tileset`: grid, solid tiles and collision rects, animated tiles, 47-blob and 16-bitmask auto-tiling terrains), loaded from a cooked map (a hand-written `.ogt` of `type tilemap`, a Tiled `.tmj` or an LDtk `.ldtk`) with og.load.tilemap and placed by an og.Tilemap component.
Layers draw through the sprite batch in 16x16-tile chunks culled to the view, each at the map's sprite layer plus its z, scrolled by its parallax; solid tiles become static og-physics colliders merged into rectangles. Runtime edits (og.tilemap.setTile, re-auto-tiling the neighbourhood) are world state (the og.tilemap state block), and the colliders follow them.
Cells count from the top-left corner, x right and y down (Tiled's); the map's top-left corner is at the entity's position.

functions.name: setTile
functions.doc: Change a cell. It applies at once to getTile, and to drawing and colliders at the og.tilemap system (this tick when called before it). Deterministic: equal edits in equal order give equal maps.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The map, the layer, the cell and the tile.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity whose map is not adopted yet, an unknown layer, a cell outside the map or a tile the tileset lacks.

functions.name: getTile
functions.doc: A cell's tile id, -1 when empty: on a terrain layer the tile auto-tiling resolved from the neighbours (setTile writes 1 or 0 there; the id changes with them). -1 outside the map or before the map is adopted.

functions.name: cellAt
functions.doc: The cell under a world point (its xy), for a map at its entity's position.

functions.name: cellCenter
functions.doc: A cell's centre in world coordinates (z of the map).

x-og-modules.name: audio
x-og-modules.doc:
Sound: inside the tick, the engine's og.audio system (after the game's systems and physics) turns AudioSource changes into a deterministic, time-stamped command stream; outside the tick the host's mixer renders it (an AudioWorklet on the web, the output device, a capture or a null sink natively).
The stream, not the PCM, is world state: snapshots, restore and the world hash cover it, and nothing a sink does reaches the world. Load sounds with og.load.sound; inserting a source plays it, setting `playing` false stops it, and a one-shot sets `playing` back to false when it ends.
Spatial gain and pan are computed in the tick from the source's og.Transform relative to the first AudioListener (three.js convention: the listener looks down -Z, +X is right; with none, the origin looking down -Z).

consts.name: SOUND_FINISHED
consts.doc: SoundEnded.reason: a one-shot played to its end.

consts.name: SOUND_STOPPED
consts.doc: SoundEnded.reason: `playing` was set to false.

consts.name: SOUND_REMOVED
consts.doc: SoundEnded.reason: the AudioSource was removed from a living entity.

consts.name: SOUND_REPLACED
consts.doc: SoundEnded.reason: `sound` changed while it played.

consts.name: SOUND_CULLED
consts.doc: SoundEnded.reason: more sources played than Audio.maxVoices and this one stood lowest (priority, then volume, then age).

functions.name: outputLatency
functions.doc:
How long after its world time a sample leaves the speaker, as the host reports it: on the web the AudioContext's baseLatency and outputLatency and the worklet ring's buffer, natively the device's latency (cpal's playback less callback instant) and the mixer's buffer; 0 headless (the null and capture sinks are driven to the tick). Host input, written to og.Audio between ticks, so a replay carries it. A rhythm game hears a note at its time plus this: judge a press against the note's time plus the latency, then a calibrated rest (the display, the hand).
Inside a system og.Audio must be among its reads or writes.
functions.returnsDoc: Seconds; 0 headless.

x-og-modules.name: nav
x-og-modules.doc:
Navigation: grids (A* and jump point search with eight-way moves that never cut a blocked corner, line-of-sight smoothing), flow fields for crowds, and navmeshes (baked at cook time from a level's static colliders and models, or built at runtime for a flat procedural level) with funnel paths and box obstacles that rebuild only the tiles they touch.
Agents are entities with an og.NavAgent (and an og.Transform): the og.nav system, after the game's systems and before physics, plans their paths, follows them and adds the og.Steering behaviours; an entity with an og.Velocity (a physics body) gets its velocity written, any other its Transform moved. Everything is deterministic and in snapshots: paths, grid edits, obstacles and flow targets.
Agents move on the profile's plane: x and y in 2D (a grid's rows run up), x and z in 3D (y kept on grids, from the surface on a navmesh).

consts.name: NAV_IDLE
consts.doc: NavAgent.status: not seeking.

consts.name: NAV_MOVING
consts.doc: NavAgent.status: following a path or a flow field.

consts.name: NAV_ARRIVED
consts.doc: NavAgent.status: within stopDistance of the target.

consts.name: NAV_UNREACHABLE
consts.doc: NavAgent.status: no path reaches the target, or the agent is off its grid or navmesh.

consts.name: NAV_PARTIAL
consts.doc: NavAgent.status: the target is cut off; moving to the reachable point nearest it.

functions.name: grid
functions.doc: A grid agents and path queries plan on. Runtime edits (og.nav.setCost) are world state.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Its size, cell size, origin and costs.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for costs of the wrong length.

functions.name: gridFromTilemap
functions.doc: A grid over a placed map: its cells, its world position (the map's top-left corner at the entity), blocked where the collision layers have solid tiles. Edits to the map later do not follow; build another.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The map's entity and the blocking layers.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.Tilemap or a map not loaded.

functions.name: setCost
functions.doc: Change a grid cell's cost (0 blocks it): agents on the grid re-plan, flow fields over it rebuild.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown grid or a cell outside it.

functions.name: cellAt
functions.doc: The grid cell under a world point.

functions.name: findPath
functions.doc: A path between two points on a grid or a navmesh, now: corners, length and whether it reaches the end.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The grid or navmesh and the two points.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown grid or navmesh, or when no path starts (an end off the grid or mesh).

functions.name: flowField
functions.doc: A flow field towards targets over a grid: one Dijkstra pass gives every cell a direction, so any number of agents (NavAgent.nav = the field) steer by a lookup. It rebuilds when the grid changes.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown grid.

functions.name: setFlowTargets
functions.doc: Move a flow field's targets (rebuilds it).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown flow field.

functions.name: flowAt
functions.doc: The direction a flow field gives at a point (unit length, or zero at a target or where nothing is reachable).

functions.name: load
functions.doc: A cooked navmesh: an `.ogt` of `type navmesh` (a scene, the boxes and the agent) baked by og cook from the scene's static colliders and models.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path that is not a cooked navmesh.

functions.name: build
functions.doc: A navmesh over a flat floor with boxes carved out, built now: for procedural levels (a level with slopes and stairs is baked at cook time with og.nav.load).

params.name: desc
params.doc: The floor, the boxes and the agent.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an empty floor.

functions.name: setObstacle
functions.doc: Set, move or (with no box) remove an obstacle on a navmesh: the spans under the box (grown by the agent radius) are blocked and only the tiles it touches, and their neighbours, are rebuilt. Agents on the mesh re-plan. World state.

params.name: id
params.doc: The obstacle's id, the game's own (a door's number).

params.name: obstacle
params.doc: The box; omitted removes the obstacle.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown navmesh.

functions.name: nearest
functions.doc: The point on a navmesh nearest a world point, within `extent` (half sizes).

params.name: extent
params.doc: The search box's half sizes; zero: 2 2 2.

functions.returnsDoc: Null when no polygon is within the box.

functions.name: pathOf
functions.doc: The path an agent follows now (its corners from where it planned), for debugging and playtests; `dump_nav:<entity>` writes the same.
functions.returnsDoc: Null for an entity that has not planned.

x-og-modules.name: ai
x-og-modules.doc:
Enemy and NPC AI as data: behaviour trees and state machines in `.ogt` files of `type behaviour` (crates/og-ai/README.md has the grammar), perception (sight cones checked against physics occlusion, hearing of spatial sounds and game noises) and a blackboard per agent.
An entity with an og.AiAgent (and an og.Transform) thinks in the og.ai system before the game's systems: perception first, then its tree or machine, whose running action moves it through its og.NavAgent (og.nav plans and walks after the game's systems) or runs one of the game's commands (GameDesc.commands, with the agent's entity handle as its first argument) before the next tick.
Conditions read blackboard keys (declared, set by actions or og.ai.set, or built in: self, position, sees, heard, target, targetPosition, targetDistance, lastSeen, sinceSeen, heardAt, sinceHeard, elapsed), the agent's component fields (`Health.hp`) and resource fields (`Game.alarm`). Deterministic; memories and blackboards are in snapshots. `dump_ai:<entity>` writes an agent's state, running node and blackboard.

consts.name: AI_RUNNING
consts.doc: AiAgent.status: the tree or state is still running.

consts.name: AI_SUCCESS
consts.doc: AiAgent.status: the tree succeeded on the last think.

consts.name: AI_FAILURE
consts.doc: AiAgent.status: the tree failed on the last think.

functions.name: load
functions.doc: A cooked behaviour (an `.ogt` of `type behaviour`, validated by og cook).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path that is not a cooked behaviour.

functions.name: parse
functions.doc: A behaviour from text, now (tests and generated behaviours; assets go through og cook).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused with the first error's line and the fix.

functions.name: get
functions.doc: A blackboard value of an agent as of its last think.
functions.returnsDoc: A number, a boolean, a point `{x, y, z}`, an entity handle, or null for an unknown key or an agent that has not thought.

functions.name: set
functions.doc: Set a blackboard value of an agent: a number, a boolean, a point `{x, y, z}` or an entity handle `{entity}`.

params.name: key
params.doc: The key; built-in keys are refused.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an agent that has not thought yet, a built-in key or another kind of value.

functions.name: noise
functions.doc: Make a noise agents may hear next tick (a gunshot, a door, a thrown stone).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a world without og.ai.

functions.name: describe
functions.doc: What an agent is doing: its state, the node it runs and the path to it, its status, its blackboard and its target.
functions.returnsDoc: Null for an entity that has not thought.

x-og-modules.name: platform
x-og-modules.doc:
Platform services as host capabilities (docs/design.md §2.8): cloud store, leaderboards, telemetry, Origin Point and AI marks. Game code names a method and its arguments, never a credential, a URL or a cookie: the host owns them. On the web the shell forwards each call to the Player through origin-checked postMessage (Player protocol 2, docs/web-export.md); natively the host answers from a local JSON store (`og run --platform-store`, default `<project>/.og/platform.json`).
Calls are asynchronous: each returns a request number at once, and the answer arrives at the start of a later tick, when og.platform sends PlatformAnswered; read it with og.platform.result. Answers are host input, like key presses: the probe's `dump_platform` lists every call, its arguments, its answer and the ticks.
Errors carry the Player's stable codes: offline, timeout, invalid, unauthorized, not_found, conflict, too_large, rate_limited, unavailable, failed; retryable is true for offline, timeout, unavailable and rate_limited.

functions.name: storeGet
functions.doc: Read one key of the player's store for this game.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed key. The answer's data is `{ key, value, revision }` (value null and revision 0 for a key never written).

functions.name: storeSet
functions.doc: Write one key of the player's store for this game; with a revision, only if nobody wrote it since (another device, another tab).

params.name: desc
params.doc: The key, the value and the revision it must be at.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed key or a value over 64 KiB. The answer's data is `{ key, revision }` (the new revision); `conflict` when the key moved past desc.revision.

functions.name: storeList
functions.doc: The keys of the player's store and their revisions.
functions.returnsDoc: The answer's data is `{ keys: [{ key, revision }] }`.

functions.name: leaderboardSubmit
functions.doc: Submit a score; the board keeps the player's best.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The board, the score and its order.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a score that is not finite. The answer's data is `{ board, rank, best }`, or `{ board, rank: null, queued: true }` while offline.

functions.name: leaderboardTop
functions.doc: The best entries of a board, and the player's own.
functions.returnsDoc: The answer's data is `{ board, order, entries: [{ rank, name, score, me }], me }`.

functions.name: leaderboardAround
functions.doc: The entries around the player's rank.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The board and how many around the player.

functions.returnsDoc: The answer's data is the leaderboardTop shape with the entries around the player's rank.

functions.name: telemetry
functions.doc: Record a game event for the game's analytics.

params.name: name
params.doc: The event: `level.started`, `level.completed`, `boss.defeated` (letters, digits, `.`, `_`; the Player files it as `game.custom.<name>`).

params.name: attrs
params.doc: Its attributes: an object of at most 16 strings (up to 512 characters), numbers, booleans or null, keys a lowercase letter then letters, digits and `_`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed name or attributes. Fire and forget: nothing answers.

functions.name: point
functions.doc: Ask for Origin Point for something the player did.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a reason outside 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`. The answer's data is `{ granted, balance }`; under a Player today always `{ granted: 0, balance: null }` (the platform grants nothing until a release carries an approved point policy), locally the amount asked.

functions.name: aiMark
functions.doc: Disclose AI-generated content the game shows.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an empty kind or label. The answer's data is `{ marked: true }`.

functions.name: loadSettings
functions.doc: Ask for the game's saved settings (volume, controls, language): store.get of the key `og.settings`. Where the Player has no store, or is offline, the shell answers from the browser's own storage; natively, from the local store.
functions.returnsDoc: The request; its answer's data is `{ key, value, revision }` (value null before the first save).

functions.name: saveSettings
functions.doc: Save the game's settings under `og.settings` (the last save wins), with the same local fallback as loadSettings.

params.name: value
params.doc: The settings: an object, at most 64 KiB encoded.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a value that is not an object or is too large.

functions.name: result
functions.doc: The answer to a call, once it arrived.
functions.returnsDoc: Null while it is in flight, or for an unknown request.

functions.name: info
functions.doc: What answers platform calls here, and what it answers.

functions.name: now
functions.doc: The host's wall-clock time, UTC milliseconds since 1970, as of this tick: what the host last told the engine (when it attached, and with every answer, applied at a tick's start like the answers) moved on by the ticks since. The one wall-clock read game code may make: it is host input, so a replay with the same answers gives the same values. Use it to know how long the game was closed (a save's time against a launch's), never to time play (that is og.Time).
functions.returnsDoc: UTC milliseconds; 0 until a host has told the time (`none`).

x-og-modules.name: i18n
x-og-modules.doc:
Localization: one string table per locale (`.ogt` of `type strings`: `locale "ja"`, its font chain `fonts "..."`, `string "key" "message"`), messages in a subset of ICU MessageFormat (`{name}`, `{n, number}`, `{n, plural, =0 {..} one {..} other {..}}` with `#`, `{g, select, a {..} other {..}}`), CLDR plural rules, and the locale the host asks for (the browser's `navigator.language` on the web, `og run --locale` natively).
The active locale is the best loaded table for the request (ja-JP takes ja; zh-TW takes zh-Hant or zh-TW), else the base table (`base true`, else en, else the first). A key it lacks is read from its `fallback` table, then the base. It also sets the UI's font chain (its fonts first, then the other tables') and direction: a right-to-left locale (ar, he, fa, ur) mirrors og.ui's layout, and og-ui shapes Arabic words with the font's own tables (a font cooked with the `arabic` charset carries them). `og cook` warns about every key a locale lacks, or takes other arguments for, than the base.

functions.name: load
functions.doc: Load a cooked string table; the active locale is negotiated again.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path that is not a cooked string table, or a font of its chain that is not cooked.

functions.name: setLocale
functions.doc: Ask for a locale (a player's choice in settings); the active one is the best table for it.

functions.name: locale
functions.doc: The requested and active locales, the direction and the font chain.

functions.name: t
functions.doc: A key's message in the active locale, formatted with its arguments; a key no table has answers the key itself and logs one warning.

params.name: args
params.doc: The arguments: an object of strings and numbers, `{ count: 3, name: "Kai" }`.

functions.name: has
functions.doc: Whether the active locale's own table has the key (not a fallback).

x-og-modules.name: ui
x-og-modules.doc:
The engine's UI: an immediate-mode toolkit. Systems describe the tree every tick with these calls; the engine lays it out Clay-style, themes it with the platform's design tokens, draws it over the frame and answers the probe (dump_ui, touch_move_to, move_to_text) from it.
The engine opens the frame before the game's systems (from og.Input and the play surface) and closes it after them, so calls belong inside systems; outside one they do nothing and log a warning. Interaction is decided against the previous tick's rectangles, which are also what the probe resolves, so a scripted touch_move_to and a click agree; response edges (clicked, changed, submitted) last one tick.
Lengths are CSS pixels of the play surface (origin top left, y down), the unit of og.Input and the probe. Ids: an element's id is unique among its siblings (`idi("Slot", 3)` is `Slot#3`); a path `Inventory/Slot#3` names it after its nearest ancestors. The UI state (hover, press, focus, caret, scroll) is world state: snapshots and the world hash carry it.

functions.name: configure
functions.doc: Set the scheme, the density and the fonts, typically in GameDesc.start. Takes effect from the next tick.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose UI is configured.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead font.

functions.name: viewport
functions.doc: This tick's play surface: the render target's size in CSS pixels, its DPR and safe area, as the host reports them.

functions.name: theme
functions.doc: The design tokens the UI draws with.

functions.name: open
functions.doc: Open a container; the calls until its close() build its children.

params.name: id
params.doc: Its id, unique among its siblings.

functions.name: openPanel
functions.doc: Open a card, closed by close(): og.ui.panel without the callback.

functions.name: openScroll
functions.doc: Open a vertical scroll container, closed by close(): og.ui.scroll without the callback.

functions.name: close
functions.doc: Close the open container.
functions.returnsDoc: Its response, for an interactive container; the zero response otherwise.

functions.name: row
functions.doc: A row built by `build`: open(id, {...desc, direction: row}), build(), close().

params.name: desc
params.doc: Its layout and look; direction is row.

functions.returnsDoc: Its response, for an interactive row.

functions.name: column
functions.doc: A column built by `build`: open(id, {...desc, direction: column}), build(), close().

params.name: desc
params.doc: Its layout and look; direction is column.

functions.returnsDoc: Its response, for an interactive column.

functions.name: panel
functions.doc: A card built by `build`: openPanel(id, desc), build(), close().

functions.name: scroll
functions.doc: A vertical scroll container built by `build`: openScroll(id, desc), build(), close().

functions.name: richText
functions.doc: A paragraph of inline spans from markup, for a string-table message (og.i18n.t) so a translation carries its own emphasis: `[b]bold[/b]` (thickened in the distance field as far as it reaches, plus a second copy one device pixel right), `[color=danger]` or `[color=#ff8800]` (a ThemeColor follows the skin), `[size=xl]` (a TypeStepName), `[font=mono]`, `[icon=coin]` (a cell of the icon atlas, one em), `[link=shop]Open the shop[/link]` (accent ink, underlined, focusable by keys and pads; a child element `<id>/shop` of kind link for the probe) and per-glyph motion `[wave]`, `[shake]`, `[pulse]` (by the tick; still under reduced motion). `[[` is a literal bracket. Lines break between the spans' words (a word restyled mid-way stays whole), each as tall as its tallest span on one baseline. Markup it cannot read shows as text and logs a warning.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Defaults for its spans: type step, ink, alignment, wrapping, width and font.

functions.name: label
functions.doc: MSDF text that wraps at its width (word breaks; between CJK characters under kinsoku, katakana words kept whole; long words between characters) unless nowrap. The probe reads its text.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Type step, ink, alignment, wrapping, width and font.

functions.name: button
functions.doc: A capsule button with a label; `clicked` is a press and a release inside it. The probe reads its label.

functions.name: image
functions.doc: A texture region, or a solid rectangle.

functions.name: progress
functions.doc: A capsule track filled to a fraction.

params.name: value
params.doc: How full it is, from 0 to 1.

functions.name: slider
functions.doc: A track with a fill and a thumb: a press anywhere on it sets the value and dragging follows. Pass back the value it answers next tick.

functions.name: toggle
functions.doc: A switch with a label; a click flips it. Pass back the state it answers next tick. The probe reads its label.

functions.name: textField
functions.doc: One line of text: a press focuses it with the caret at the press and a drag selects; typed text (og.input's TextInput events, else the keys) replaces the selection at the caret; Backspace, Delete, arrows, Home and End edit, Shift with them selects; Ctrl or Cmd with A selects all, with C copies and with X cuts (the page's clipboard, through the shell); an input method's composition shows underlined at the caret until it commits; Enter submits and leaves, Escape leaves. The text scrolls to keep the caret in view and the caret blinks by the tick (steady under reduced motion). Pass back the text it answers next tick. The probe reads its text, or the placeholder while empty.

functions.name: textArea
functions.doc: Several lines of text: textField's editing, with Enter starting a new line, Up and Down moving between lines and Home and End to a line's ends, the text wrapped between words at the area's width and scrolled to keep the caret's line in view. Pass back the text it answers next tick. The probe reads its text, or the placeholder while empty.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Placeholder, width, rows and length limit.

functions.name: tooltip
functions.doc: A tooltip for the element just built: shown below it (above without room) once the pointer has rested on it for the slow motion duration, drawn over everything. The probe reads its text.

functions.name: idi
functions.doc: The id of the index-th of several siblings of one name: `idi("Slot", 3)` is `Slot#3`.

functions.name: breakpoint
functions.doc: The size class of the play surface of the frame being built (desktop outside a frame).

functions.name: frameViewport
functions.doc: The play surface of the frame being built: og.ui.viewport without the world, for code that only builds UI.

functions.name: hasIcon
functions.doc: Whether the icon atlas has an icon of this name (templates draw a fallback otherwise).

functions.name: seconds
functions.doc: The UI's clock in seconds: frames built over the tick rate (simulation time, never the wall clock).

functions.name: frameTheme
functions.doc: The design tokens of the frame being built: og.ui.theme without the world, for code that only builds UI (the templates).

functions.name: openAnchor
functions.doc: Open an anchored group, closed by close(): og.ui.anchor without the callback.

params.name: id
params.doc: Its id; the probe path is the id alone.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Where it sits and how it lays out.

functions.name: anchor
functions.doc: An anchored group built by `build`: a layer at a point of the safe area, over the tree, for HUD corners and touch controls.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Where it sits and how it lays out.

functions.name: openTransition
functions.doc: Open a transition container (a column), closed by close(); build its children only while the answer is visible: it stays visible while it leaves. Its content takes no input while it moves.

functions.name: transition
functions.doc: Content that enters and leaves: fade, slide or scale by the tick from the motion tokens. `build` runs while it is visible.

functions.name: openModal
functions.doc: Open a dialog, closed by closeModal(); build its content only while the answer is visible. The probe sees the backdrop as `<id>` and the panel as `<id>/Panel`.

functions.name: closeModal
functions.doc: Close a dialog opened with openModal (its panel and backdrop).

functions.name: modal
functions.doc: A dialog built by `build` while visible: scrim, centred panel, focus kept inside, Back and the backdrop dismiss it unless locked. Set your open flag false on `dismissed`.

functions.name: spotlight
functions.doc: A spotlight over everything (a tutorial step): the scrim on four sides of the hole, an amber edge around it. Presses on the dimmed parts stop there (clicked); presses in the hole reach what is under it. Shades are `<id>/Top`, `Left`, `Right`, `Bottom`; the hole is `<id>/Hole`.

params.name: hole
params.doc: The rectangle to leave lit, as og.ui.bounds answers; null dims everything.

functions.name: bounds
functions.doc: Where an element was in the last frame, by id or `Parent/Child` path (topmost first), as touch_move_to resolves it.

functions.name: openList
functions.doc: Open a virtualised list (a scroll column) and learn which rows to build: listItem(i) and close() for each, then closeList().

functions.name: openGrid
functions.doc: Open a virtualised grid and learn which cells to build: gridItem(i) and close() for each, then closeList().

functions.name: listItem
functions.doc: Open row `index` of the open list (`Row#index`): selectable and focusable; its content follows until close(). A press that started on one row and is released on this one answers `dropped`.

functions.name: gridItem
functions.doc: Open cell `index` of the open grid (`Cell#index`): a slot on fill, focusable; its content follows until close(). Drops answer `dropped` as listItem's.

params.name: selected
params.doc: Drawn selected (fill-strong with an amber bar).

functions.name: closeList
functions.doc: Close a list or grid opened with openList or openGrid.

functions.name: dragging
functions.doc: The row or cell a held press started on in the list or grid of this id (built under the same parent): a drag in progress, to draw what is dragged under the pointer.

functions.name: list
functions.doc: A virtualised list built by `build(index)` for the rows in view.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Row count, size and the selected row.

functions.name: grid
functions.doc: A virtualised grid built by `build(index)` for the cells in view.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Cell count, size, columns and the selected cell.

functions.name: tabs
functions.doc: A segmented control: a neutral track, the chosen tab on the thumb. Tabs are `Tab#i` and the probe reads their labels.

params.name: selected
params.doc: The chosen index from game state.

functions.name: select
functions.doc: A select: a field-like trigger with the chosen label and a chevron; a press or Activate opens its menu `<id>.menu` (options `Option#i`) under it, a focus scope; choosing closes it with changed. Back or a press outside closes it.

params.name: selected
params.doc: The chosen index from game state.

functions.name: stepper
functions.doc: A number stepper: `Dec`, `Value`, `Inc`. The buttons step within the range; Left and Right step it while a button is focused.

functions.name: radio
functions.doc: A radio group of `Option#i` rows: a ring, filled amber when chosen, and a label.

params.name: selected
params.doc: The chosen index from game state.

functions.name: checkbox
functions.doc: A checkbox with a label; a press flips it.

functions.name: checkboxList
functions.doc: Checkboxes in a column (`Option#i`).

functions.name: chip
functions.doc: A chip: a capsule on fill; selected inverts to fg. For filters and tags.

functions.name: badge
functions.doc: A badge: a small status capsule in its tone.

functions.name: divider
functions.doc: A hairline in the border colour across its parent.

functions.name: spacer
functions.doc: Empty space.

params.name: size
params.doc: Its size along both axes; null grows into the free space.

functions.name: keyValue
functions.doc: A key (fg-muted) and its value (fg, at the end) on one row: stats, settings summaries, receipts.

params.name: mono
params.doc: The value in the monospaced font (prices, ids).

functions.name: skeleton
functions.doc: A skeleton: the neutral fill standing in for content that is loading, with a sheen that passes every 1.6 s (still under reduced motion).

functions.name: spinner
functions.doc: A loading spinner: eight dots around a circle, the bright one turning by the tick.

params.name: size
params.doc: Its diameter in CSS px; 0 is the small control height.

functions.name: icon
functions.doc: An icon of the atlas (UiDesc.icons) by name; an unknown name draws an empty slot and warns. The probe reads the name.

functions.name: meter
functions.doc: A health, mana or xp bar. A drop shows at once and leaves a pale trail that follows after a beat; a rise grows into place with a ghost of the target; both by the tick.

functions.name: cooldown
functions.doc: A cooldown: a disc whose amber ring fills clockwise from the top as it runs out, bright and full when ready, a label or icon in the middle. A press reports clicked (ready or not).

params.name: remaining
params.doc: How much of the cooldown is left, 0 to 1: 1 just used, 0 ready.

functions.name: minimap
functions.doc: A mini-map frame: the map in a border-strong frame, markers as dots (the player amber and ringed), an N mark and a zone label.

functions.name: dialogue
functions.doc: A dialogue box: a portrait slot, the speaker in amber ink and the line typed out by the tick. A press or Activate while typing shows the whole line; once shown it answers advanced. The line is `<id>/Body/Line` and the probe reads what is shown.

functions.name: joystick
functions.doc: A virtual joystick: a base and a knob that follows a press that started on it. It keeps the finger that grabbed it (any of og.Pointers), so another finger can hold an action button at the same time.

functions.name: dpad
functions.doc: A d-pad of four arms (`Up`, `Down`, `Left`, `Right`), each at least 44 CSS px.

functions.name: actionButton
functions.doc: A round touch action button: pressed while held (jump, fire), clicked on a tap; at least 44 CSS px.

params.name: text
params.doc: Its label (and what the probe reads).

functions.name: toast
functions.doc: Queue a toast: it stacks at UiDesc.toastAnchor, enters, stays its time and leaves; at most three are up (older ones leave first); a press dismisses it. Callable anywhere (systems, commands, start); it is world state, so snapshots carry it.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose UI shows it.

functions.returnsDoc: Its id, for dismissToast.

functions.name: dismissToast
functions.doc: Start a toast's exit.

functions.name: navigate
functions.doc: Queue a navigation intent for the next tick: a gamepad og.Input does not read yet, a custom binding, a command.

functions.name: back
functions.doc: Escape or gamepad B this tick, not taken by a dialog or menu: true once, then taken. A pause screen closes on it.

functions.name: setPlayers
functions.doc: Local multiplayer: how many players this screen takes (1 to 4; 1 by default). Pads 1 to count - 1 each move a focus of their own among the same controls, shown as a ring in the player's colour (info, success, warn), and their A presses the control under it (Response.pad says which pad); pad 0 shares the one focus with the keyboard and the pointer, and Back and adjusting a slider stay pad 0's. Declare it every tick the screen shows; it takes effect from the next tick, and a dialog's focus scope holds every pad's focus inside it.

functions.name: focus
functions.doc: The path of the control pad pad's focus is on in the last frame (pad 0: the shared focus of the pointer, keyboard and pad 0), as touch_move_to resolves it; empty when it is on none.

params.name: pad
params.doc: The pad, 0 to 3; past 3 answers empty.

functions.name: a11y
functions.doc: The accessibility tree of the last frame: every element with a role, its name, value, states and bounds, and the focus order Tab walks. A shell mirrors it into the page for screen readers; a playtest reads the same fields on dump_ui's elements.

functions.name: setNavigation
functions.doc: Whether keyboard and gamepad navigation moves focus on this screen (on by default). A gameplay HUD whose keys move the player turns it off; an open dialog or menu turns it back on while it is open. Takes effect from the next tick.

functions.name: memory
functions.doc: A number the UI keeps for an id under the open element (a template's tab, a count-up's start tick), in snapshots like the rest of the UI state. Read it every tick it is used: an unused memory is dropped.

params.name: id
params.doc: The id, unique among its siblings' memories.

functions.name: remember
functions.doc: Set a number memory (see memory).

functions.name: tick
functions.doc: Frames the UI has built: its clock, for animations by the tick.

functions.name: counter
functions.doc: A number label that counts (ease-out cubic, by the tick) from where it was to the value each time the value changes, grouped with commas; a skin with motion.pop bumps it when it lands. Scores, currency, rewards.
functions.returnsDoc: The number shown this tick.

functions.name: burst
functions.doc: Throw rays and sparks from the element built just before (a star landing, a reward), once, from when it first appears. Off under reduced motion.

functions.name: shake
functions.doc: Shake the element built just before, from this tick (a wrong answer, a locked door, a refused purchase): call it once, on the tick it happens; the element swings and comes to rest by itself, and snapshots carry it. Still under reduced motion. A refused press on a disabled button already shakes when the skin's motion.shake is set.

functions.name: screenTransition
functions.doc: A transition between game screens drawn over the whole frame (through the overlay, over every other UI layer). Pass the screen the game wants every tick and build the one it answers: when the wanted screen changes the cover closes over the old screen for half the duration, the answer switches, and the cover opens on the new one. Deterministic by the tick; snapshots carry it; under reduced motion every kind is a fade.

params.name: screen
params.doc: The screen the game wants now.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Kind, duration, colour or texture, side.

functions.name: previewViewport
functions.doc: Lay the UI out for another play surface (a phone in portrait at 3x, a notch) until cleared with null: for headless previews and playtests of responsive layouts. Render at width x dpr by height x dpr (`og run --size`).

params.name: viewport
params.doc: The surface to lay out for; null returns to the host's.

functions.name: mainMenu
functions.doc: The title screen template. Returns the item chosen this tick.

functions.name: pauseMenu
functions.doc: The pause screen template: a dialog with Resume first; Back answers `resume`.

functions.name: settingsScreen
functions.doc: The settings template: Audio (volumes, mute), Graphics (quality, frame rate, reduced motion, contrast), Controls (sensitivity, invert, vibration, bindings) and Language. Pass the settings in every tick and keep what it answers.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Open, the settings, languages and hooks.

functions.name: platformerHud
functions.doc: The platformer HUD template.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Lives, coins, score, level and timer.

functions.name: shooterHud
functions.doc: The shooter HUD template.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Health, armor, ammo, abilities and map.

functions.name: puzzleHud
functions.doc: The puzzle HUD template.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Level, score, target, stars, moves and timer.

functions.name: idleHud
functions.doc: The idle and incremental HUD template: answers `tap` and `buy:<id>` actions.

functions.name: racingHud
functions.doc: The racing HUD template.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Speed, gear, laps, place, times and boost.

functions.name: cutscene
functions.doc: The dialogue and cutscene template: letterbox, the dialogue box, Skip.

functions.name: shopScreen
functions.doc: The shop template.

functions.name: inventoryScreen
functions.doc: The inventory template: a grid of slots with drag and drop.

functions.name: levelSelect
functions.doc: The level select template.

functions.name: resultsScreen
functions.doc: The results template: stars, the score counting up, the best, stats, actions and Share.

functions.name: leaderboardScreen
functions.doc: The leaderboard template.

functions.name: tutorialOverlay
functions.doc: The onboarding template: a spotlight and a callout per step.

functions.name: loadingScreen
functions.doc: The loading template.

functions.name: confirmDialog
functions.doc: The confirm dialog template.

functions.name: alertDialog
functions.doc: The alert template. Returns true the tick it is dismissed.

callbacks.name: UiBuild
callbacks.doc: Builds a container's children: ui calls made inside it nest under the container.

callbacks.name: UiItemBuild
callbacks.doc: Builds one row or cell of a virtualised list or grid: ui calls made inside nest under it.

callbacks.name: UiAction
callbacks.doc: A template's action, by its id (a menu item, `buy:<item>`, `share`).

callbacks.name: SettingsChanged
callbacks.doc: The settings after a change: persist them (cloud save, local storage through the shell) and apply them.

x-og-modules.name: systems
x-og-modules.doc: Systems the engine ships as TypeScript: game-level code, listed explicitly in GameDesc.systems like the game's own, so the schedule (and dump_world) shows them and nothing runs that the game did not ask for.

values.name: cameras
values.doc: The camera controllers, in this order: og.orbitCamera (og.OrbitCamera), og.followCamera (og.FollowCamera) and og.follow2D (og.Follow2D). Each moves og.Camera only while an entity carries its component. List them before the game's systems that read og.Camera: `systems: [...og.systems.cameras, ...yours]`.

x-og-modules.name: commands
x-og-modules.doc:
The command channel: actions scheduled on simulation time, from `og run --commands "t:action[:args];..."` or the probe's commands().
Core actions ship with the engine; a module or a game registers more. Unknown actions warn and continue. Not in publish builds.

functions.name: register
functions.doc: Register an action into the command channel. GameDesc.commands does this for a game's own actions.

params.name: name
params.doc: The action name, snake_case, such as `spawn_wave`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a name a core action or another registration already uses.

functions.name: parse
functions.doc: Parse a script without scheduling it.
functions.returnsDoc: The steps, or the first malformed step.

functions.name: help
functions.doc: Every action the channel knows: core actions in CoreAction order, then registered ones by name.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose channel is asked.

functions.name: schedule
functions.doc: Schedule a script on simulation time, from the current tick.
functions.returnsDoc: The report, or the first malformed step.

callbacks.name: CommandHandler
callbacks.doc: A registered action. It runs at the start of the tick it was scheduled for.

params.name: args
params.doc: The `:`-separated arguments after the action name.

x-og-modules.name: probe
x-og-modules.doc:
The probe: RuntimeProbe protocol 5 (origin/packages/contracts/src/probe.ts) served natively, plus the engine's wire members.
In a page it is published on globalThis.__runtime_probe__; on native, `og` serves it as JSON-RPC 2.0 over a loopback WebSocket at /probe.
A refusal is false or null exactly as protocol 5; a JSON-RPC error is only for a malformed call or an unknown method.
Probe entity ids are entity names; an unnamed entity is `#<index>.<generation>`.

consts.name: PROBE_GLOBAL
consts.doc: The global the page publishes the probe on.

consts.name: PROBE_VERSION
consts.doc: The RuntimeProbe contract revision both sides speak.

consts.name: PROBE_WIRE_VERSION
consts.doc: The wire revision hello reports.

consts.name: REPLAY_SEED_PARAM
consts.doc: The page query parameter that starts a deterministic replay from a uint32 seed.

consts.name: PLAYTEST_MAX_TICKS
consts.doc: The longest playtest one request may advance, in fixed steps.

consts.name: PROBE_PROGRAM_MAX_OPERATIONS
consts.doc: The most operations one probe program may carry.

interfaces.name: RuntimeProbe
interfaces.doc: RuntimeProbe protocol 5, member for member. Every member answers synchronously with JSON-serialisable values.

members.name: version
members.doc: PROBE_VERSION.

members.name: tick
members.doc: Fixed steps the world has taken since load.

members.name: state
members.doc: A JSON snapshot: the fixed timings head, then the game's own facts.

members.name: advance
members.doc: Take whole fixed steps regardless of the wall clock.
members.returnsDoc: The tick after the steps.

members.name: pause
members.doc: Hold the wall-clock loop; advance still steps.

members.name: resume
members.doc: Release the wall-clock loop.

members.name: input
members.doc: One event through the input layer's own path.
members.returnsDoc: False is a refusal.

members.name: accepted
members.doc: Page events (keyboard, pointer, wheel) the input layer accepted since load.

members.name: pick
members.doc: What is under a point of the play surface.
members.returnsDoc: Null when nothing is under the point.

members.name: entity
members.doc: One entity's published parameters: its tunable fields as `Component.field` keys.
members.returnsDoc: Null for an unknown entity.

members.name: bounds
members.doc: The ranges of one entity's tunable fields, from the schema.
members.returnsDoc: Null for an unknown entity.

members.name: patch
members.doc: Move one tunable field for this run only; it applies within one frame. The probe never writes project files.
members.returnsDoc: False is a refusal.

The frame of the current tick, rendered offscreen and read back as a PNG.

On the web the readback is asynchronous: through the request ring the answer arrives when the copy completes; a synchronous in-page call answers null on the first tick and the frame from then on (a capture is requested on tick N and answered on N + 1).

x-og-modules.name: terrain
x-og-modules.doc:
Terrain (phase 2): a height field over a rectangle, cooked by `og cook` from a `type terrain` .ogt (a 16-bit grey PNG or an EXR heightmap, an optional control map, up to four layered materials with slope and altitude rules) into tiles; drawn as a geometry clipmap around the camera (nested levels by distance, no cracks) that casts and receives shadows under the fog; collided with as a height field; baked into navmeshes by a navmesh file's `terrain` entry.
Load it with og.terrain.load, then place it: an og.Terrain on an entity draws it placed by the entity's world transform (centred on its position, turned and scaled with it), and an og.Collider of shape SHAPE_HEIGHTFIELD naming the TerrainInfo's geometry makes it solid. og.TerrainScatter grows grass, flowers or stones over a layer near the camera. og.terrain.sample answers the surface's height and normal anywhere (pass it the entity's position, quaternion and scale); og.terrain.edit raises, lowers, flattens, smooths or paints it at runtime, and og.terrain.setLayer retunes a layer. Edits are world state: a snapshot keeps them, the world hash covers them, and a restore brings the ground back as it was (rebuilt from the cook with the restored edits replayed, for the renderer, physics and sample alike).
Its tiles stream (phase 3): the cook stores the field as a pyramid of tiles, each compressed on its own, and every frame the renderer keeps on the GPU only the tiles the camera's clipmap wants, within each terrain's tile budget (16 MiB by default), decoded off the frame (a worker thread natively, the browser's DecompressionStream on the Web) a few at a time, the most needed first; until a tile arrives its area draws from the coarser level that holds it, then fades in. Nothing a tick reads depends on which tiles are resident (collision and og.terrain.sample read the whole field), so a run's world hash is the same streamed or not. The probe's `terrain_stream:resident` decodes every wanted tile before each frame instead (`terrain_stream:stream[:<MiB>]` streams again, within that budget), and `dump_stream`'s `terrain` gives the tiles resident, waiting, decoding and cached.

functions.name: load
functions.doc: Load a cooked terrain (a `type terrain` .ogt under assets/) and its layers' textures, and register its height field with physics under TerrainInfo.geometry. Loading the same path again answers the same terrain.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path that is not a cooked terrain, or a layer texture that does not load.

functions.name: sample
functions.doc: The surface under a world point: its height, normal and slope. Callable inside systems (it reads the terrain, not the world).

params.name: desc
params.doc: The terrain, where it stands and the point.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown terrain.

functions.name: bounds
functions.doc: A terrain's box in world space when it stands at `origin`, turned by `quaternion` and scaled by `scale` (its entity's world transform): the box around its turned corners.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown terrain.

functions.name: edit
functions.doc: Change a terrain under a round brush: raise, lower, flatten or smooth its heights (the renderer, physics and og.terrain.sample see the change from the next frame and tick), or paint a layer into its control map (making one when it has none).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown terrain, a layer beyond its layers, or a brush that misses it.

functions.name: layer
functions.doc: A terrain's layer as it is now (for a tuning tool: read it, change it, setLayer it).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown terrain or layer.

functions.name: setLayer
functions.doc: Replace a terrain's layer look and rules (its textures stay). Drawn from the next frame.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown terrain or layer.

x-og-modules.name: stream
x-og-modules.doc:
Asset streaming groups (phase 3): a scene's `stream "<name>" { asset ...; distance x y z r [unload d] | volume "<entity>"; priority n }` blocks name glTF models (without skins or morph targets), textures and sounds that load and unload together, and what loads them: the camera within `r` of the anchor (kept until it is past `unload`, 1.25 r by default), the camera inside the named entity's box (its position ± half its scale, turned with it), or neither (og.stream.request only). `og cook` packs each group's files into `cooked/stream/<name>.ogb`; `og build --publish` ships the packs beside the boot bundle, which the shell and the service worker fetch first, and fetches a pack only when its group loads.
At every tick boundary the engine decides which groups are wanted, admits them by priority (then name) within the memory budget (256 MiB by default; GPU textures and meshes and decoded audio, as the cook measured them), evicting lower-priority resident groups to make room for a higher one, and reads and puts in place at most one group's assets per boundary. A group that cannot fit waits, queued; one larger than the whole budget fails. Until its group is resident, a model draws its proxy (its coarsest LOD, untextured), a texture is a 1x1 grey placeholder and a sound plays as silence of its own length; then the real ones take over the same handles. Physics always collides with the proxy's meshes and a sound's length never changes, so nothing a tick reads depends on what is resident: a run's world hash is the same streamed or not.
Every change of a group's state sends StreamEvent at the start of the next tick; og.stream.status and og.stream.budget answer at once, and the probe's `dump_stream` lists the budget, the memory used and its peak, every group (trigger, state, why, since which tick), the recent changes and the terrain streamer's tiles.

consts.name: STREAM_UNLOADED
consts.doc: `StreamEvent.state`: the group is unloaded (StreamState unloaded).

consts.name: STREAM_QUEUED
consts.doc: `StreamEvent.state`: the group waits for room in the budget (StreamState queued).

consts.name: STREAM_LOADING
consts.doc: `StreamEvent.state`: the group's pack is being read (StreamState loading).

consts.name: STREAM_RESIDENT
consts.doc: `StreamEvent.state`: the group's assets are in place (StreamState resident).

consts.name: STREAM_FAILED
consts.doc: `StreamEvent.state`: the group failed (StreamState failed; og.stream.status says why).

functions.name: status
functions.doc: One streaming group's state.

params.name: group
params.doc: The group's name, as its scene declares it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a group no scene declares.

functions.name: request
functions.doc: Ask for a group (any trigger) until og.stream.release: it loads from the next tick boundary, within the budget by its priority.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a group no scene declares.

functions.name: release
functions.doc: Stop asking for a group; it unloads at the next tick boundary unless its trigger still wants it.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a group no scene declares.

functions.name: budget
functions.doc: The memory budget, what the groups take now, the peak and every group.
functions.returnsDoc: The budget and the groups; refused only for a world that does not exist.

functions.name: setBudget
functions.doc: Set the memory budget from the next tick boundary; a lower one evicts the lowest-priority groups until the rest fit.

params.name: bytes
params.doc: The bytes resident groups may take.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a negative or non-finite size.
