OrbitCamera.description:
Orbits og.Camera around the entity carrying it, as three.js OrbitControls: a left-button drag on the play surface turns it, the wheel zooms, autoRotate turns it on its own.
Camera controllers are game-level systems the engine ships in TypeScript (og.systems.cameras); list them in GameDesc.systems: `systems: [...og.systems.cameras, ...yours]`. The first entity carrying one, in query order, drives the camera.
The camera sits `distance` from the orbited point (the entity's position plus `target`) in the direction given by `azimuth` about +Y and `polar` from +Y, and looks at the point. Every angle is computed with deterministic arithmetic, so a replay moves the camera identically on every host.

polar.description: The angle from +Y: near 0 looks straight down, half pi is level with the point.

maxPolarAngle.description: The largest polar angle a drag reaches, as three.js OrbitControls.maxPolarAngle.

rotateSpeed.description: Drag sensitivity, as three.js OrbitControls.rotateSpeed: at 1, dragging the play surface's height turns a full circle.

zoomSpeed.description: Wheel sensitivity, as three.js OrbitControls.zoomSpeed: at 1, 100 CSS pixels of wheel change the distance by a tenth.

pointer.description: Controller state: where the pointer was on the previous tick of a drag.

FollowCamera.description: Chases the entity carrying it with og.Camera: a third-person 3D view that eases towards a point offset from the entity and looks at it. Driven by og.systems.cameras; the first entity carrying one, in query order, drives the camera.

offset.description: Where the camera sits relative to the entity: in the entity's own axes with followRotation, else in world axes.

lookOffset.description: The point the camera looks at, relative to the entity's position.

followRotation.description: Turn the offset with the entity's rotation, so the camera stays behind it.

smoothTime.description: Roughly how long the camera takes to catch up with a moved entity; 0 snaps it there every tick.

Follow2D.description: Keeps og.Camera on the entity carrying it in the xy plane, for 2D games: the camera moves only when the entity leaves the dead zone, eases by smoothTime (smoothTimeY for y when set) and, with clamp, stays inside the bounds; lookAhead leads it in the direction the entity moves. The camera keeps its z, rotation and projection. Driven by og.systems.cameras; og.CameraZone entities then keep the view inside the zone the entity is in.

offset.description: Where the camera centre sits relative to the entity.

deadZone.description: Half the width and height of the box around the camera centre inside which the entity moves without moving the camera.

smoothTime.description: Roughly how long the camera takes to catch up; 0 snaps it every tick.

smoothTimeY.description: The same for y alone (a platformer follows jumps more lazily than runs); below 0 uses smoothTime.

lookAhead.description: Lead the entity by its velocity times this many seconds (0: no look-ahead).

lookAheadMax.description: The largest lead along x and y.

lookAheadSmoothing.description: Roughly how long the lead takes to turn when the entity does.

last.description: Controller state: the entity's position on the previous tick.

clamp.description: Keep the camera centre between boundsMin and boundsMax.

boundsMin.description: The smallest x and y the camera centre takes with clamp.

boundsMax.description: The largest x and y the camera centre takes with clamp.

CameraZone.description: A rectangle of the xy plane (min to max, world units, not moved by the entity's Transform) that keeps a 2D view inside it while the entity followed by og.Follow2D is in it: rooms, arenas, a level's bounds. Of overlapping zones the highest priority wins, then the first in query order. The engine's og.camera system picks the zone after the game's systems (into og.Camera's zone fields); entering another zone scrolls the view across over the new zone's scrollTime, or jumps when it is 0. A zone smaller than the view centres it.

scrollTime.description: Seconds the view takes to scroll from the zone the entity left into this one (a room transition, eased in and out); 0 jumps at once. Visual only: the camera resource records the transition, so replays scroll the same.

CameraRail.description: Moves og.Camera along a spline through p0 to p(points - 1) (Catmull-Rom, through every point) to the point nearest the entity carrying it, easing by smoothTime: a corridor, a side-scroller's track, a 3D chase on rails. A perspective camera looks at the entity; an orthographic one keeps its z and rotation. Applied by the engine's og.camera system after the game's systems.

points.description: How many of p0...p7 the rail uses (2 to 8).

smoothTime.description: Roughly how long the camera takes to catch up along the rail; 0 snaps.

Geometry.description: Vertex and index data, as three.js BufferGeometry. Comes from a loaded glTF.

Side.description: Which faces are drawn, as three.js FrontSide, BackSide and DoubleSide.

RenderTier.description: The backend the renderer runs on; the probe's hello reports it.

x-og-variants.webgpu: WebGPU in a browser: the full feature set.
x-og-variants.webgl2: The WebGL2 fallback: no compute, CPU culling and particles, tiled lights.
x-og-variants.vulkan-cpu: Native Vulkan on a CPU rasterizer (Mesa lavapipe or llvmpipe, SwiftShader): the executors' sandboxes. Frame times there say nothing about a player's GPU.
x-og-variants.none: No renderer: frames are not produced and capture refuses.

Antialias.description: Antialiasing, as og-render's Antialias. RenderCapabilities.antialias reports what the device resolved.

x-og-variants.tier: The tier's method: TAA on the full tier (WebGPU, Metal, Vulkan), 4x MSAA on WebGL2.
x-og-variants.msaa4: 4x MSAA on any tier: sharp sprites and text, no temporal blur; off where the HDR format cannot be multisampled.
x-og-variants.taa: Temporal antialiasing on any tier: a sub-pixel jitter per frame and a reprojected history; converges over about eight frames.

RenderOptions.description: How the renderer is created for a game (GameDesc.render). The host reads it once, when it attaches the renderer.

shadowMapSize.description: The side of each of the directional light's three cascade maps, in texels; smaller saves memory on phones (three 2048 maps are 64 MB).

StandardMaterialDesc.description:
A physically based metallic-roughness material with three.js MeshStandardMaterial parameter names.
It is og-render's reflected StandardMaterial field for field: metalnessMap and roughnessMap read a glTF metallic-roughness texture (blue metal, green rough), so give both the same texture; alphaTest above 0 discards below that alpha; transparent blends, sorted back to front.
The stylised fields: unlit (three.js MeshBasicMaterial), toon with its gradientMap ramp, a rim (fresnel) light, a hit flash, dissolve with a glowing edge, and a per-material outline. All are off at their defaults.
The MeshPhysicalMaterial fields, under three.js's names and glTF's KHR_materials_* meanings, all off at their defaults: clearcoat with clearcoatMap, clearcoatRoughnessMap and clearcoatNormalMap; sheen (velvet, cloth) with sheenColor, sheenRoughness and their maps; transmission (glass, water) refracting the opaque scene behind through thickness, attenuationColor and ior; iridescence (soap film, oil) with its film's iridescenceIOR and iridescenceThicknessRange; anisotropy (brushed metal) along anisotropyRotation or anisotropyMap. They draw on every tier, WebGL2 included; unlit and toon materials ignore them.
A transmissive material is drawn after the opaque scene, back to front with the transparent ones, and refracts what was drawn before it (not other transmissive or transparent objects); thickness is in the mesh's own units, scaled with it.
normalMap is read in glTF's tangent frame: red tilts towards +u, green up the image. The tangents come from the model (the cook generates MikkTSpace ones where a glTF has none) or are generated when the geometry is made; normals follow a non-uniform scale correctly.

metalnessMap.description: Metalness from the texture's blue channel.

roughnessMap.description: Roughness from the texture's green channel.

aoMap.description: Ambient occlusion from the texture's red channel.

emissiveIntensity.description: A multiplier on the emitted colour.

opacity.description: The opacity; below 1 only with transparent.

transparent.description: Blend instead of writing opaque pixels.

alphaTest.description: Discard pixels whose alpha is below this.

normalScale.description: How strongly the normal map bends the normal, per tangent axis.

aoMapIntensity.description: How strongly aoMap darkens the ambient light.

unlit.description: No lighting at all, as three.js MeshBasicMaterial: the colour (times map) plus emissive.

toon.description: Cel shading, as three.js MeshToonMaterial: light is quantized by gradientMap (three built-in bands without one), highlights are hard.

gradientMap.description: The toon ramp: a texture whose first row maps the light's angle (left dark, right lit) to the light received, read without filtering.

rimColor.description: Rim (fresnel) light added at grazing angles, unshadowed (linear).

rimIntensity.description: The rim light's strength; 0 is none.

rimPower.description: How tight the rim is (higher: thinner).

flashColor.description: The colour a hit flash mixes towards (linear, may exceed 1).

flash.description: How far the final colour is mixed towards flashColor (0 none, 1 flat): animate it per tick for a hit flash.

dissolve.description: The dissolved fraction: 0 whole, 1 gone. Pixels whose noise is below it are discarded (shadows too); the band just above glows with dissolveEdgeColor.

dissolveMap.description: The dissolve noise from the texture's red channel; without one, value noise over the object-space position.

dissolveEdgeColor.description: The glowing edge (linear, usually above 1 so it blooms).

dissolveEdgeWidth.description: The width of the glowing band in noise units.

dissolveScale.description: The frequency of the built-in noise (cells per object-space unit).

outlineWidth.description: This material's outline width in pixels; 0 is none (PostEffects.outline outlines everything).

clearcoat.description: A clear lacquer over the surface, as three.js MeshPhysicalMaterial.clearcoat: a second, 4 % reflective specular layer on the surface's normal before normalMap (car paint, varnished wood, wet plastic); 0 is none.

clearcoatRoughness.description: How rough the clear coat is, as three.js MeshPhysicalMaterial.clearcoatRoughness.

clearcoatMap.description: The coat's strength from the texture's red channel, times clearcoat (MeshPhysicalMaterial.clearcoatMap).

clearcoatRoughnessMap.description: The coat's roughness from the texture's green channel, times clearcoatRoughness.

clearcoatNormalMap.description: A tangent-space normal map of the coat alone; the base keeps normalMap (MeshPhysicalMaterial.clearcoatNormalMap).

clearcoatNormalScale.description: How strongly clearcoatNormalMap bends the coat's normal, per tangent axis.

sheen.description: A velvet-like layer that brightens grazing angles (cloth, fuzz, peach skin), as MeshPhysicalMaterial.sheen: its strength, times sheenColor; 0 is none.

sheenColor.description: The sheen's colour (linear), times sheenColorMap; black is none.

sheenRoughness.description: How rough the sheen is: low keeps it to a thin rim, high spreads it over the surface.

sheenColorMap.description: The sheen's colour from the texture's RGB (sRGB).

sheenRoughnessMap.description: The sheen's roughness from the texture's alpha channel.

transmission.description: How much light passes through, as MeshPhysicalMaterial.transmission (glass, water, thin plastic): the opaque scene behind is refracted and blurred by roughness; 0 is none. Unlike opacity, the surface keeps its reflections.

transmissionMap.description: Transmission from the texture's red channel.

thickness.description: The volume's thickness under the surface in the mesh's own units (glTF KHR_materials_volume): how far refraction bends the view and how much attenuationColor absorbs; 0 is a thin wall.

thicknessMap.description: Thickness from the texture's green channel.

attenuationDistance.description: The distance light travels in the volume before it is tinted to attenuationColor (world units); 0 is no absorption, three.js's Infinity.

attenuationColor.description: The colour white light becomes after attenuationDistance in the volume (linear).

ior.description: The index of refraction (glTF KHR_materials_ior): the reflectance of a dielectric, ((ior - 1) / (ior + 1))^2 (4 % at 1.5), and how far transmission refracts.

iridescence.description: A thin-film interference layer, as MeshPhysicalMaterial.iridescence (soap bubbles, oil, beetle shells); 0 is none.

iridescenceThicknessRange.description: The film's thickness in nanometres: x where iridescenceThicknessMap is black, y where it is white and everywhere without the map (three.js's [100, 400]).

iridescenceMap.description: Iridescence from the texture's red channel.

iridescenceThicknessMap.description: The film's thickness between iridescenceThicknessRange's ends from the texture's green channel.

anisotropy.description: Stretches the specular highlight along a direction of the surface, as MeshPhysicalMaterial.anisotropy (brushed metal, hair, satin); 0 is none, 1 fully stretched. Needs the geometry's tangents (generated when it has none).

anisotropyRotation.description: The stretch's direction in radians from the tangent (+u) towards the bitangent.

anisotropyMap.description: The stretch's direction in red and green (-1 to 1 in the tangent frame, turned by anisotropyRotation) and its strength in blue, times anisotropy.

Mesh.description:
Draws a geometry with a material at the entity's MatrixWorld, as a three.js Mesh.
The material is a handle from og.render.standardMaterial or from a loaded glTF (GltfInfo.materials); its StandardMaterialDesc maps to the renderer as that struct's docs say.

flash.description: A hit flash: the lit colour mixed towards flashColor by this much (og.tween.flash fades it out). Drawn through a copy of the material per flash level (16 levels).

DirectionalLight.description:
The sun, as three.js DirectionalLight: parallel light along the entity's local -Z (aim it with transform.lookAt, as a camera). The first one found is drawn, with three shadow cascades.
Without one, the renderer's default sun (from above and to the side, intensity 3) lights the scene.

intensity.description: The radiance multiplier, as three.js DirectionalLight.intensity.

castShadow.description: Cast shadows through three cascades, as three.js Light.castShadow.

shadowDistance.description: How far from the camera shadows reach; they fade over the last tenth. Smaller is sharper.

PointLight.description:
A light shining in every direction from the entity's position, as three.js PointLight. Its radiance at distance d is color * intensity / d^2, faded smoothly to zero at distance.
Lights are clustered (Forward+): each pixel shades only the lights whose distance reaches it, so hundreds are cheap. Lights out of view are skipped; up to MAX_LIGHTS in view are drawn, and past that (or past what one screen cluster holds, MAX_CLUSTER_LIGHTS) the ones brightest at the camera are kept. The first two in view with castShadow get cube shadows.

distance.description: Where the light reaches zero, as three.js PointLight.distance (never infinite here).

SpotLight.description: A cone of light along the entity's local -Z, as three.js SpotLight.

intensity.description: The radiance at one metre on the axis.

angle.description: The half-angle of the outer cone, as three.js SpotLight.angle.

penumbra.description: The fraction of the cone over which the light fades out, as three.js SpotLight.penumbra.

RenderSettings.description: The frame's look after lighting: environment light, sky, bloom, exposure metering and tone mapping. Read after each tick; it never feeds back into the simulation. Camera.exposure is the manual exposure.

environmentIntensity.description: The strength of the image-based ambient light from the procedural sky.

sky.description: Draw the procedural sky behind the scene instead of Camera.background.

bloom.description: Light above the threshold bleeds into its surroundings.

bloomThreshold.description: Brightness after exposure where bloom starts; 1 is display white.

bloomKnee.description: Softens the threshold over threshold plus or minus knee; 0 is a hard cut.

bloomIntensity.description: How much of the blurred light is added back.

autoExposure.description: Meter every frame to middle grey (deterministic: the current frame only), then apply Camera.exposure as compensation.

toneMapped.description: ACES tone mapping; false clamps, so 2D colours come out exactly as authored at exposure 1.

decalAtlas.description: The texture Decal components take their uvMin to uvMax region from; 0 draws decals as solid colour.

Lut.description: A colour lookup table for PostEffects.lut, from og.load.lut (a `.cube` file).

ParticleEmitter.description: A particle emitter asset for ParticleSystem.emitter, from og.load.emitter (an `.ogt` of `type particles`).

x-og-variants.auto: GTAO on the full tier, SSAO on WebGL2.
x-og-variants.gtao: Ground-truth ambient occlusion (3 slices): the better looking one.
x-og-variants.ssao: Hemisphere SSAO with 8 samples: the cheaper one.

DofQuality.description: How many taps depth of field gathers per pixel.

x-og-variants.high: 48 taps at half resolution: rounder, smoother bokeh.

SpriteBlend.description: How a sprite is blended over what is below it.

x-og-variants.additive: Added (light, fire, magic): order-independent within a layer.

StripBlend.description: How a trail, ribbon or beam is blended.

x-og-variants.alpha: Alpha blended: smoke trails, tyre marks.

PostEffects.description:
The post stack beyond RenderSettings' bloom, exposure and tone mapping, and camera shake. Every effect is off by default (its switch false or its amount 0) and then costs nothing: no pass is recorded. Read after each tick; it never feeds back into the simulation.
Screen-space ambient occlusion, outlines, depth of field, motion blur and god rays run a depth-normal prepass, turned on with them. Grading, vignette, aberration, grain and the flash apply to the display colour after tone mapping; the UI and screen-space sprites (the overlay) come after all of it.

ao.description: Screen-space ambient occlusion: darkens the ambient light in creases and contact areas.

aoRadius.description: The world-space radius searched for occluders.

outline.description: Outlines every opaque surface from depth and normal edges (materials with outlineWidth get theirs anyway).

outlineWidth.description: Line width in pixels, drawn inside the silhouette.

outlineDepthThreshold.description: The relative depth step that counts as a silhouette (0.04 is 4 %).

outlineNormalThreshold.description: The normal change that counts as a crease (1 - cos of the angle; 0.4 is about 53 degrees).

depthOfField.description: Bokeh depth of field: pixels away from the focus distance blur into discs.

dofFocusDistance.description: The distance from the camera that is sharp.

dofFocusRange.description: The half-width of the sharp band around it.

dofMaxBlur.description: The largest blur radius, as a fraction of the image height (0.012 is about 9 px at 720p).

dofFalloff.description: How quickly blur grows outside the band: full blur focusRange times (1 + falloff) away.

motionBlur.description: Per-object and camera motion blur along the screen-space velocity.

motionBlurShutter.description: The shutter as a fraction of the frame (0.5 is a 180 degree shutter).

godRays.description: Screen-space light shafts from the DirectionalLight (the sun must be in front of the camera).

godRaysDecay.description: How fast the rays fade along their length.

godRaysDensity.description: How far towards the sun each ray samples (a fraction of the distance).

godRaysTint.description: A linear tint on the light the rays carry.

godRaysThreshold.description: Sky brightness (linear, before exposure) below which the sky carries no rays.

glow.description: Order-independent 2D glow: sprites with SpriteDesc.glow (and 2D particles with a glow) are blurred and added back, with or without bloom.

glowIntensity.description: How much of the blurred glow is added back.

lut.description: Colour grading by a lookup table from og.load.lut; 0 is none.

lutIntensity.description: 0 leaves the image as tone mapped, 1 applies the table fully.

vignette.description: Darkened (or tinted) edges of the frame.

vignetteRadius.description: Where darkening starts, as a fraction of the half-diagonal.

vignetteColor.description: The linear colour the edges move towards.

chromaticAberration.description: Red and blue split towards the edges, in pixels at the corners at 720p; 0 is off.

filmGrain.description: Luminance-weighted noise amplitude in display units, a new pattern every tick (0.04 is subtle); 0 is off.

flash.description: A full-screen flash: the display colour mixed towards flashColor by this much (animate it per tick); 0 is off.

shakeTrauma.description: Camera shake held at a fixed level (decay it yourself): 0 none, 1 the most (the amplitude is trauma squared). Prefer og.camera.shake, which decays by itself; the frame shakes by the larger of the two. Smooth value noise by the tick, so a replay shakes the same. Visual only.

shakeMaxOffset.description: The largest offset at trauma 1, as a fraction of the view height.

Lighting2D.description: 2D lighting of the sprite layers minLayer to maxLayer: their colour is multiplied by ambient plus every Light2D reaching the pixel, shadowed by Occluder2Ds and sprites with castShadow. Other layers (and the overlay) are drawn as authored. Off by default.

ambient.description: Light everywhere (0 is darkness outside the lights).

maxLayer.description: The highest lit sprite layer (above it: UI and HUD layers stay unlit).

resolution.description: The light map's resolution as a fraction of the target.

Light2D.description: A light in the 2D plane at the entity's position (z ignored): color times intensity at its centre, falling to zero at radius with (1 - d/r)^falloff, shadowed by occluders when castShadows. Lighting2D.enabled turns 2D lighting on; at most 64 are drawn.

radius.description: Where the light reaches zero, in world units.

sourceRadius.description: The light's own size: larger gives softer shadows.

castShadows.description: Occluders between the light and a pixel shade it.

Occluder2D.description: A rectangle that blocks 2D light (walls, crates, characters), centred on the entity's position and turned with it about z. Pixels inside it are not shadowed by it. At most 128 are drawn.

height.description: Its height in world units.

Decal.description: A projected decal (scorch marks, blood, posters, bullet holes): the entity's unit box (-0.5 to 0.5 on each axis, scaled by its Transform) projected along its local -Z onto every lit opaque surface inside it, shaded with the surface. Its image is the uvMin to uvMax region of RenderSettings.decalAtlas (a solid colour without one). At most 32 are drawn.

color.description: A linear colour multiplied with the atlas.

uvMin.description: The atlas region's top-left corner, v down.

uvMax.description: The atlas region's bottom-right corner, v down.

emissive.description: Linear light added where the decal covers (glowing runes, lava).

roughness.description: The surface roughness under the decal; -1 keeps the surface's.

angleFade.description: Surfaces turned further than this from the projection direction are not covered (the last 15 degrees fade).

ParticleSystem.description: Emits particles from an og.load.emitter asset at the entity's MatrixWorld. Particles are simulated by the renderer from (seed, startTick, the tick), so they are deterministic and replay, and never feed back into the simulation: compute on the full tier, the CPU on WebGL2, identical either way.

seed.description: The random seed: systems with different seeds differ.

startTick.description: The tick emission started: write og.world tick when spawning a one-shot burst.

stopTick.description: The tick emission stops (the particles live out); 0 keeps emitting while the emitter loops.

visible.description: Whether it is drawn (a hidden system loses its particles).

Trail.description: A streak behind the entity: its world positions over the last `lifetime` seconds as a camera-facing strip, from widthStart and color at the head to widthEnd and colorEnd at the tail.

lifetime.description: How long a position stays in the trail.

minDistance.description: A new point is kept when the head has moved this far.

color.description: The linear colour at the head; above 1 blooms.

colorEnd.description: The linear colour at the tail.

texture.description: A texture along the strip; 0 is solid.

uvTile.description: The texture repeats every this many world units; 0 stretches it once over the length.

layered.description: Draw it in the 2D sprite order at `layer` (a sprite's trail over a tile background) instead of with the 3D scene.

layer.description: With layered: the sprite layer it is drawn in, before that layer's sprites.

Beam.description: A strip from the entity's position to `end` whose texture scrolls with the tick: lasers, tethers, lightning (jitter).

end.description: The far end, in world space.

texture.description: A texture along the beam; 0 is solid.

tile.description: Texture repeats per world unit along the beam.

scroll.description: Texture scroll in repeats per second.

segments.description: Segments: 1 is straight, more let jitter bend it.

jitter.description: Sideways jitter in world units, new every tick (lightning).

RibbonDesc.description: An explicit camera-facing strip through points, drawn this frame only (immediate mode, as og.render.sprite): submit it every tick it should show.

points.description: The points, in order (at least two).

texture.description: A texture along the strip; null is solid.

uvTile.description: The texture repeats every this many world units; 0 stretches it once.

TextDesc.description: A line or block of MSDF text in the world's xy plane facing +z, drawn this frame only (immediate mode: submit it every tick it should show).

font.description: The font from og.load.font; null draws nothing.

text.description: The text; `\n` starts a new line.

position.description: The baseline origin of the first line.

size.description: The em size in world units.

layer.description: Draw order among sprites and text; higher draws on top.

align.description: How each line sits on `position`: start puts its left end there, center its middle, end its right end.

outline.description: World text: an outline around the glyphs, as a fraction (0 to 1) of the widest the font's distance range allows (a font cooked with a larger px_range takes thicker outlines).

screen.description: Draw in screen space over the finished frame: position is the first baseline's origin in CSS pixels from the top left, y down, size in CSS pixels, rotation clockwise.

clip.description: Screen text: cut to [x, y, width, height] in CSS pixels, per pixel; null draws it whole.

TextMeasureDesc.description: Text to measure with og.render.measureText, laid out as og.render.text lays it out.

text.description: The text; `\n` starts a new line.

size.description: The em size in world units.

TextMetrics.description: The extent of a laid-out text, in world units.

height.description: Lines times the font's line height.

SpriteDesc.description: A textured or solid quad in the world's xy plane facing +z, drawn this frame only (immediate mode, as og.render.text): submit it every tick it should show. Sprites and text are sorted by layer and drawn over the 3D scene.

texture.description: The texture from og.load.texture; null draws a solid quad of the colour.

height.description: Its height in world units.

anchor.description: The point of the quad at `position`, as a fraction of its size from the bottom-left corner: (0.5, 0.5) is the centre.

color.description: A linear colour multiplied with the texture.

uv.description: The texture region drawn, [u0, v0, u1, v1] with v down; null is the whole texture (a sheet's frame for animation).

layer.description: Draw order among sprites and text; higher draws on top.

flash.description: A hit flash: the colour mixed towards flashColor by this much, keeping the alpha.

glow.description: Strength in the 2D glow buffer (PostEffects.glow); 0 none.

castShadow.description: Block 2D light (Lighting2D) with the sprite's rectangle.

flipX.description: Mirror the region left to right.

flipY.description: Mirror the region top to bottom.

sortY.description: Within its layer, draw by y: lower on the screen draws in front (top-down games).

slice.description: Nine-slice: [left, top, right, bottom] insets in texture pixels of the region; the corners keep their size (sliceScale world units per pixel), edges and centre stretch. null draws it whole.

sliceScale.description: Nine-slice: world units (CSS pixels on screen) per texture pixel of the insets.

screen.description: Draw in screen space over the finished frame instead of the world: position x, y in CSS pixels from the top left with y down, width and height in CSS pixels, anchor from the top left, rotation clockwise; never tone mapped, blurred or depth tested (a HUD). flash, glow, blend and castShadow apply to world sprites only.

clip.description: Screen sprites: cut to [x, y, width, height] in CSS pixels; null draws it whole.

Sprite.description:
A sprite drawn every frame at the entity's MatrixWorld (its xy and z, its rotation about z; its scale multiplies width and height, so squash and stretch is a tween of og.Transform.scale). With an og.Flipbook on the entity, the texture, region and anchor come from the flipbook's current frame.
Sorted with the immediate sprites and text by layer, then (sortY) by y, then texture: one draw per run of one texture. Tile layers draw before the sprites of their layer.

texture.description: The texture (og.load.texture); 0 draws a solid quad of the colour.

width.description: Its width in world units (times Transform.scale.x).

height.description: Its height in world units (times Transform.scale.y).

anchor.description: The point of the quad at the entity's position, as a fraction from the bottom-left corner: (0.5, 0) stands it on its feet. A flipbook frame's pivot replaces it.

color.description: A linear colour multiplied with the texture.

uvMin.description: The texture region's top-left corner, v down.

uvMax.description: The texture region's bottom-right corner, v down.

layer.description: Draw order among sprites, tiles and text; higher draws on top.

sortY.description: Within its layer, lower y draws in front: top-down characters, props and trees overlap by their feet.

flipX.description: Mirror left to right (a character facing left).

flash.description: A hit flash: the colour mixed towards flashColor by this much (og.tween.flash fades it out).

glow.description: Strength in the 2D glow buffer (PostEffects.glow); 0 none.

castShadow.description: Block 2D light (Lighting2D) with the sprite's rectangle.

sliceX.description: Nine-slice: the left and right insets in texture pixels of the region (0 0 with sliceY 0 0 draws it whole). World panels, health bars, speech bubbles.

sliceY.description: Nine-slice: the top and bottom insets in texture pixels.

sliceScale.description: Nine-slice: world units per texture pixel of the insets.

shadow.description: A soft blob shadow on the ground under the sprite's anchor, this dark (0 none, 0.4 typical), drawn under every sprite of its layer.

shadowSize.description: The blob's width and height; 0 0 is 0.8 by 0.3 of the sprite's width.

shadowOffset.description: The blob's centre relative to the anchor.

Afterimage.description: Ghosts of the entity's og.Sprite: every `interval` ticks its pose (position, rotation, scale, frame, flips) is kept, and the last `count` are drawn behind it, fading from `opacity` to 0, tinted by color. A dash, a speed-up, a teleport. The history is world state (the og.sprite state block).

color.description: A linear tint (above 1 with additive, a glow).

additive.description: Add the ghosts instead of blending them.

active.description: Record new ghosts; false lets the existing ones fade out.

FloatingTextDesc.description: A damage number or pickup text that pops at a point, rises, spreads and fades by itself (no per-tick submission). Deterministic: its drift comes from the tick and its order, and it is world state (the og.sprite state block).

text.description: The text, such as `-12` or `+1 key`.

position.description: Where it appears (above a hit, usually).

font.description: The font; null uses the UI's body font.

size.description: The em size in world units.

outline.description: The outline's width as a fraction of the font's distance range (0 none).

rise.description: How far it climbs over its life.

spread.description: The largest sideways drift, left or right.

fade.description: The last part of its life it fades over.

pop.description: How much bigger it starts, settling to its size in the first fifth of its life.

crit.description: A critical hit: critScale times bigger, a stronger pop.

BoxGeometryDesc.description: A box centred at the origin, as three.js BoxGeometry(width, height, depth).

height.description: Its extent along y.

PlaneGeometryDesc.description: A rectangle in the xy plane facing +z, centred at the origin, as three.js PlaneGeometry(width, height); turn it -pi/2 about x for a floor.

height.description: Its extent along y.

SphereGeometryDesc.description: A UV sphere centred at the origin, as three.js SphereGeometry(radius, widthSegments, heightSegments).

RenderCapabilities.description: What the renderer can do on this device. Backend limits are reported here, never by missing members.

compute.description: Whether compute passes run (GPU culling, GPU particles).

antialias.description: The antialiasing the device resolved RenderOptions.antialias to.

maxLights.description: How many point and spot lights one frame draws (MAX_LIGHTS on every tier).

maxShadowedLights.description: How many point and spot lights may cast shadows.

width.description: The render target width in device pixels.

height.description: The render target height in device pixels.

Shader.description: A material shader from og.load.shader (an `.ogt` of `type shader`): WGSL hooks of the lit shader and the parameters they read.

Asset.description: A loaded bundle, scene or glTF asset.

Font.description: A cooked MSDF font: its glyph table and one or more atlas pages.

Sound.description: A cooked sound: QOA-encoded PCM the audio module plays.

Skin.description: A cooked UI skin: its atlas, fonts, icons and sounds loaded with it, for og.ui.configure.

GltfDesc.description: How to load a glTF, as three.js GLTFLoader options where they apply.

castShadow.description: Set Mesh.castShadow on every mesh instantiated from it.

receiveShadow.description: Set Mesh.receiveShadow on every mesh instantiated from it.

geometries.description: Its geometries, in glTF mesh-primitive order.

materials.description: Its materials, in glTF order, then the default material.

animations.description: Its animation clip names (the cook counts clips and does not cook them yet, so this is empty).

path.description: The cooked directory it was opened from.

FontInfo.description: A loaded font's metrics, in em units unless stated.

pages.description: Atlas pages; the renderer draws one page per pass with one shared layout.

pxRange.description: The distance range in atlas pixels.

lineHeight.description: Ascender minus descender plus the line gap.

Model.description: Draws a loaded glTF's default scene at the entity's world transform: every mesh node with its glTF material. Scene entities with a `model` line get one; world.instantiate of a glTF asset spawns one.

path.description: The path it was loaded from.
The path it was loaded from.

RigidBody.description:
A body the physics step simulates. It needs an og.Transform and usually has an og.Collider; a dynamic body without an og.Velocity gets one.
Changing a RigidBody, a Collider or Transform.scale rebuilds the body (it loses its contacts' warm starts); a Transform or Velocity that game code changed moves it (a teleport).

kind.description: BODY_DYNAMIC (0, simulated and written back), BODY_STATIC (1, never moves) or BODY_KINEMATIC (2, moved by game code through its Transform).

mass.description: Mass; 0 derives it from the collider's density and volume.

linearDamping.description: How fast linear velocity decays (0: none).

angularDamping.description: How fast angular velocity decays (0: none).

gravityScale.description: Multiplies Physics.gravity for this body: 0 floats, 1 is normal.

lock.description: Locked axes, a sum of the LOCK_* bits: 1, 2, 4 no translation along x, y, z; 8, 16, 32 no rotation about x, y, z (2D uses 1, 2 and 32).

ccd.description: 1 enables continuous collision detection, for fast small bodies that must not tunnel; 0 off.

Collider.description: The shape an entity collides with, attached to its RigidBody (or, without one, a static collider at its Transform). Sizes are scaled by og.Transform.scale.

shape.description: One of the SHAPE_* codes: 0 box, 1 sphere (a circle in 2D), 2 capsule, 3 cylinder (3D), 4 convex hull of `mesh` (a polygon in 2D), 5 triangle mesh of `mesh` (3D), 6 the height field `mesh` (3D: a terrain).

size.description: Full extents of a box, as three.js BoxGeometry(width, height, depth).

radius.description: Radius of a sphere, circle, capsule or cylinder.

height.description: A capsule's distance between its cap centres (three.js CapsuleGeometry length); a cylinder's height.

mesh.description: The geometry whose vertices a convex or triangle-mesh shape uses: a loaded glTF's geometry (registered automatically) or one given to og.physics.setMesh; for SHAPE_HEIGHTFIELD, a terrain's height field (og.terrain.load's TerrainInfo.geometry).

offset.description: Position of the shape relative to the entity.

rotation.description: Rotation of the shape relative to the entity.

friction.description: Coulomb friction (0 is ice, 1 rubber); a pair uses the mean of both colliders.

restitution.description: Bounciness (0 no bounce, 1 elastic); a pair uses the mean of both colliders.

sensor.description: 1 makes this a sensor: it reports SensorEntered and SensorExited and pushes nothing; 0 a solid.

layers.description: The collision layers this collider is on, as bits.

mask.description: The layers it collides with, as bits. Two colliders interact when each one's layers meet the other's mask.

Velocity.description: Linear and angular velocity. Written for dynamic bodies every tick (added to them by the step when missing), read for kinematic ones; set it to launch or stop a body.

linear.description: The linear velocity (2D uses x and y).

angular.description: The angular velocity about each axis (2D uses z).

Physics.description: The physics settings of the world. The profile is the project's; the same components serve both profiles.

profile.description: PROFILE_2D (2: rapier2d, the xy plane, rotation about z) or PROFILE_3D (3: rapier3d), from project.ogt. Set the other one at run time to change profile: the next step builds that profile's simulation from the components (contacts, joints' warm starts, ropes, cloth, fluids and ragdoll bodies start again), so a 3D game can play a 2D scene and back.

gravity.description: The acceleration of every dynamic body, times its gravityScale; 2D uses x and y.

substeps.description: Physics steps per tick, each of dt / substeps: more is stiffer stacks and less tunnelling, at more cost.

restSpeed.description: A dynamic body touching something, supported with at most 2 mm of overlap and slower than this before and after a step, keeps its pose and loses its residual velocity (the same number in m/s and rad/s); 0 disables it.

CollisionStarted.description: Two solid colliders started touching during the tick.

a.description: The entity with the lower id.

b.description: The entity with the higher id.

point.description: The deepest contact point in world space (z is 0 in 2D).

normal.description: The contact normal, from a towards b.

CollisionEnded.description: Two solid colliders stopped touching, or one of them went away.

a.description: The entity with the lower id.

b.description: The entity with the higher id.

SensorEntered.description: A collider started overlapping a sensor.

sensor.description: The entity whose collider is the sensor.

SensorExited.description: A collider stopped overlapping a sensor, or one of them went away.

sensor.description: The entity whose collider is the sensor.

Contact.description: One pair in contact at the end of a step, sent every tick for every touching pair: how a game asks what is touching what right now.

a.description: The entity with the lower id.

b.description: The entity with the higher id.

sensor.description: 0 for two solids; an overlap with a sensor otherwise: 1 a is the sensor, 2 b is, 3 both are.

Joint.description: A joint between two bodies (or a body and a point of the world). The component may sit on one of the bodies (`body` 0) or on an entity of its own, so one body can have several joints. Anchors are in each body's frame (rotated and moved with it, not scaled); without `other` the second anchor is a world point. A joint whose bodies are not both `og.RigidBody` entities does nothing until they are.

kind.description: JOINT_FIXED 0, JOINT_REVOLUTE 1 (hinge), JOINT_PRISMATIC 2 (slider), JOINT_SPRING 3, JOINT_ROPE 4, JOINT_BALL 5.

body.description: The first body; 0 is this entity.

other.description: The second body; 0 joins the first one to the world at `otherAnchor`.

anchor.description: Where the joint sits on the first body, in its frame.

otherAnchor.description: Where it sits on the second body, in its frame (a world point without `other`).

axis.description: The hinge or slide axis in the first body's frame (a hinge in 2D turns about z).

limits.description: Whether `min`..`max` bound the hinge angle (rad) or the slide (m).

min.description: The lower limit: radians for a hinge, metres for a slider.

motor.description: MOTOR_NONE 0, MOTOR_VELOCITY 1 (drive at motorTarget speed), MOTOR_POSITION 2 (spring to motorTarget).

motorTarget.description: The motor's target speed (rad/s, m/s) or angle or position (rad, m).

motorStiffness.description: A position motor's stiffness; a velocity motor's strength.

motorMaxForce.description: The most force (or torque) the motor applies; 0 is unbounded.

length.description: A rope's longest distance between the anchors.

collide.description: Whether the two bodies still collide with each other.

value.description: Written: the hinge angle (rad) or the slide (m) after the step; the anchors' distance for springs and ropes.

CharacterController.description: A kinematic character (3D, or top-down 2D): the entity's capsule (or any og.Collider) moved by `move` each tick, sliding along walls, climbing slopes up to `maxSlope` and steps up to `stepHeight`, snapped to the ground, carried by the moving platform it stands on and falling by gravity. The entity needs an og.Transform and an og.Collider; the step makes it a kinematic body and pushes dynamic bodies it walks into.

move.description: The wanted velocity across the ground (m/s, world space; y is ignored unless gravityScale is 0). Set it every tick.

jump.description: Held to jump: a jump starts on the tick it becomes true while grounded (or in coyote time).

jumpSpeed.description: The upward speed of a jump.

gravityScale.description: Multiplies og.Physics.gravity; 0 for top-down movement in any direction.

maxSlope.description: The steepest slope it walks up.

stepHeight.description: The highest step it climbs without jumping (0: none).

snapDistance.description: How far below it the ground still holds it (stairs down, slopes): 0 lets it leave every edge.

skin.description: The gap kept between it and every surface.

coyoteTime.description: After leaving an edge, a jump still starts within this time.

pushBodies.description: Push dynamic bodies it walks into.

grounded.description: Written: standing on walkable ground after the step.

sliding.description: Written: sliding down a slope steeper than maxSlope.

velocity.description: Written: the velocity it moved at this tick (the platform's carry included).

groundNormal.description: Written: the ground's normal (zero in the air).

coyote.description: Written: seconds left in which a jump may still start (coyote time).

jumpWasHeld.description: Written: `jump` as the last step saw it (a jump starts on its rising edge).

ground.description: Written: the entity it stands on (0 in the air); a moving one carries it.

PlatformerController.description: A 2D platformer character (the 2D profile): run, jump and fall with designer units (jump height and time to apex, not gravity), coyote time, jump buffering, variable jump height (releasing jump while rising cuts the jump), apex hang, air jumps, wall slide and wall jump, one-way platforms (colliders on `oneWayLayers` are solid from above only; hold `down` to drop through), moving platforms (it rides what it stands on) and corner correction (a jump that clips a ceiling corner by less than `cornerCorrection` slides past it). The entity needs an og.Transform and an og.Collider (a box or capsule); it becomes a kinematic body.

moveX.description: The run input, -1 (left) to 1 (right). Set it every tick.

jump.description: Held to jump: a press is buffered for jumpBuffer; releasing while rising cuts the jump.

down.description: Held to drop through a one-way platform.

acceleration.description: How fast it reaches maxSpeed on the ground.

deceleration.description: How fast it stops on the ground without input.

airDeceleration.description: Deceleration in the air without input.

jumpHeight.description: How high a full jump goes.

timeToApex.description: How long a full jump takes to reach its height (sets gravity and the jump speed).

fallGravity.description: Gravity multiplier while falling (snappier landings above 1).

jumpCut.description: Gravity multiplier while rising with jump released (variable jump height; 1 disables it).

apexGravity.description: Gravity multiplier near the apex while jump is held (hang time; 1 disables it).

apexThreshold.description: The vertical speed below which the apex multiplier applies.

coyoteTime.description: After running off an edge, a jump still starts within this time.

jumpBuffer.description: A jump pressed this long before landing starts on landing.

airJumps.description: Extra jumps in the air (1: a double jump).

wallJumps.description: Slide down walls it pushes against (and jump off them).

wallSlideSpeed.description: The fastest slide down a wall.

wallJump.description: A wall jump's velocity: x away from the wall, y up.

wallJumpLock.description: After a wall jump, the run input is ignored for this long (so it leaves the wall).

oneWayLayers.description: The collision layers that are one-way platforms (solid from above), as bits.

cornerCorrection.description: How far a rising jump is nudged sideways past a ceiling corner (0: never).

maxSlope.description: The steepest slope it runs up.

snapDistance.description: How far below it the ground still holds it (slopes, small drops).

skin.description: The gap kept between it and every surface.

grounded.description: Written: standing on ground after the step.

onWall.description: Written: -1 sliding on a wall to its left, 1 to its right, 0 none.

facing.description: Written: -1 facing left, 1 right (the last run direction).

velocity.description: Written: the velocity after the step (the platform's carry excluded).

jumping.description: Written: rising from a jump (until the apex or a release cut).

airJumpsLeft.description: Written: air jumps left before landing.

coyote.description: Written: seconds of coyote time left.

buffer.description: Written: seconds a buffered jump press stays valid.

wallLock.description: Written: seconds the run input stays locked after a wall jump.

dropTime.description: Written: seconds one-way platforms stay passable after dropping through.

jumpWasHeld.description: Written: `jump` as the last step saw it.

ground.description: Written: the entity it stands on (0 in the air); a moving one carries it.

CharacterEvent.description: Something a CharacterController or PlatformerController did this step: the hooks for dust, squash, sounds and camera kicks. Read the next tick.

kind.description: CHARACTER_JUMPED 1, LANDED 2, WALL_JUMPED 3, AIR_JUMPED 4, LEFT_GROUND 5, BUMPED 6.

speed.description: The vertical speed at the moment (a landing's impact speed is negative).

Vehicle.description: A car on a dynamic chassis (the entity's og.RigidBody and og.Collider). 3D: a raycast car with four wheels (suspension, grip, steering on the front axle); its forward is the chassis's local +z (three.js Object3D.lookAt aims +z). 2D: two wheel bodies on sprung wheel joints (front at +x), driven by a motor. The wheels are not entities: og.physics.vehicleWheels gives their poses for drawing.

throttle.description: The accelerator, -1 (reverse) to 1. Set it every tick.

wheelBase.description: The distance between the front and rear axles.

track.description: The distance between the left and right wheels (3D).

mountHeight.description: The height of the wheel mounts below the chassis centre.

suspensionTravel.description: How far the suspension compresses or extends from rest.

grip.description: The tyres' grip (3D: the friction slip; 2D: the wheels' friction).

engineForce.description: The engine's force at full throttle (3D: per driven wheel, N; 2D: the motor's torque).

maxSpeed.description: The top speed: the engine's force fades out towards it (throttle against the motion brakes first).

brakeForce.description: The brakes' force at full brake.

maxSteer.description: The front wheels' largest steering angle (3D).

wheelMass.description: The wheels' mass (2D: the wheel bodies; 3D ignores it).

speed.description: Written: the forward speed (m/s; negative reversing).

contacts.description: Written: how many wheels touch the ground.

Rope.description: A Verlet rope: `segments` links from the entity's position (plus `offset`) to `end` (an entity, plus `endOffset`) or hanging free, swung by gravity and wind, colliding with every solid collider at `radius`. It moves nothing (one-way: a rope joint ties bodies together, og.Joint JOINT_ROPE). Its points are world state (the og.physics state block); og.physics.ropePoints reads them and the renderer draws the rope as a strip of `width` and `color`.

segments.description: The number of links (points minus one).

offset.description: The start's offset from the entity's position (world axes).

end.description: The entity the far end is tied to; 0 leaves it free.

endOffset.description: The far end's offset from `end`'s position.

iterations.description: Constraint passes per step: more is stiffer, at more cost.

damping.description: How much of its velocity each point keeps per tick (1: none lost).

radius.description: The thickness it collides at (0: no collision).

Cloth.description: A Verlet cloth: a `columns` × `rows` grid of points, `spacing` apart, hanging from the entity's position (its top-left corner, the grid laid out along the entity's local x and down -y), pinned by `pins` (pinned points follow the entity), with stretch and shear constraints, gravity, wind, collision against every solid collider and, with `thickness`, against itself. One-way like og.Rope; its points are world state. Drawn as a double-sided mesh with `material` (og.render.standardMaterial; 0: a plain cloth colour).

spacing.description: The rest distance between neighbouring points.

pins.description: Which points are pinned, a sum of PIN_* bits (1 top row, 2 top corners, 4 left column, 8 top rings).

damping.description: How much of its velocity each point keeps per tick.

wind.description: A steady acceleration (wind); the cloth flutters with it.

gust.description: How much the wind varies over the cloth and the tick (0: steady).

radius.description: The thickness it collides at (0: no collision).

thickness.description: Self-collision: how far apart its points keep from the points of the cloth that are not their near neighbours (0: none). About `spacing` keeps a cloth that folds or piles up from passing through itself.

substeps.description: Simulation steps per tick, each integrating and then solving `iterations` passes; with self-collision enough that a point moves less than `thickness` per step (a point moves at most half the thickness a step).

friction.description: How much of its sliding a point touching a solid loses each step (0: it slides freely; near 1 it sticks where it lands, so a cloth lowered onto the floor folds instead of spreading).

material.description: The material it is drawn with (og.render.standardMaterial); 0 is a plain cloth.

Fluid2D.description: A 2D particle fluid (any profile, in the xy plane): `count` particles spawned in a `size` box centred on the entity, simulated with double density relaxation (Clavet et al. 2005: pressure, near pressure, viscosity) on a fixed grid in a fixed order, so it is deterministic and part of the og.physics state block. Particles collide with every solid collider (pushed out of bodies; they push nothing back) and stay inside `bounds` around the entity when it is set. Fluids of one `group` interact: by `density` they layer, by `mixing` they blend. Drawn as metaballs: the particles blurred into a field the renderer thresholds into one surface of `color`, on sprite layer `layer`.

count.description: How many particles (spawned when the component appears or count changes).

size.description: The spawn box, centred on the entity.

bounds.description: The container around the entity (0 0: none; colliders still hold it).

radius.description: The interaction radius: particles closer than this push and drag each other.

restDensity.description: The density it settles at (neighbours within radius, weighted).

stiffness.description: The pressure's strength (above about 0.15 it gets springy, then unstable).

nearStiffness.description: The near pressure's strength (keeps particles apart, gives surface tension).

group.description: Fluids sharing a group above 0 push, drag and (by `mixing`) mix with each other as one fluid, at most four to a group (in entity order; a fifth is simulated alone), and are drawn as one surface whose colour follows the mix; 0 keeps the fluid to itself.

density.description: How heavy its particles are against the group's other fluids: a heavier fluid sinks under a lighter one.

mixing.description: How readily it mixes with the group's other fluids: 0 keeps them apart in layers (the boundary held), 1 blends them where they touch (their mix, colour and weight even out).

seed.description: The seed of the spawn jitter.

blobScale.description: The drawn size of each particle's blob (times radius).

threshold.description: The field value where the surface starts (higher: thinner, separate drops).

layer.description: The sprite layer it is drawn on.

Fluid3D.description: A 3D particle fluid (the 3D profile): `count` particles spawned in a `size` box centred on the entity, simulated with double density relaxation (Clavet et al. 2005: pressure, near pressure that gives surface tension, viscosity) over a spatial hash in a fixed order, so it is deterministic and part of the og.physics state block. Particles collide with every solid collider, the terrain's height field included (pushed out; they push nothing back), and stay inside `bounds` around the entity when it is set. An emitter adds particles at `emitRate` up to `maxCount`; a sink box removes those that enter it. Fluids of one `group` interact: by `density` they layer, by `mixing` they blend. Drawn as a screen-space surface: the particles' depth smoothed into one surface, refracting what is behind by its thickness and reflecting the sky, lit by the scene's lights. Cost: about 0.9 ms of CPU a tick for 2000 particles at 1 substep, 1.8 ms at 2 (native and wasm alike), growing with the particles; keep a scene's fluids to a few thousand particles. The surface costs about 1.1 ms of GPU (an Apple M4 Pro, the fluid covering a third of a 1280×720 frame) whatever the particle count, growing with the pixels it covers.

count.description: How many particles to spawn in the box (when the component appears or count or seed changes; 0: none, the emitter fills it).

size.description: The spawn box, centred on the entity.

bounds.description: The container around the entity (0 on an axis: open on that axis; colliders and the terrain still hold it).

radius.description: The interaction radius: particles closer than this push and drag each other. Cost grows with the particles, not the radius.

restDensity.description: The density it settles at (neighbours within radius, weighted).

stiffness.description: The pressure's strength (above about 0.05 it jitters, then springs apart).

nearStiffness.description: The near pressure's strength (keeps particles apart, gives surface tension).

viscosity.description: Linear viscosity (it also calms the surface; honey above 1).

group.description: Fluids sharing a group above 0 push, drag and (by `mixing`) mix with each other as one fluid, at most four to a group (in entity order; a fifth is simulated alone); 0 keeps the fluid to itself.

density.description: How heavy its particles are against the group's other fluids: a heavier fluid sinks under a lighter one.

mixing.description: How readily it mixes with the group's other fluids: 0 keeps them apart in layers (the boundary held), 1 blends them where they touch (their mix, colour and weight even out).

substeps.description: Simulation steps per tick (each costs a full pass over the particles).

seed.description: The seed of the spawn and emitter jitter.

maxCount.description: The most particles alive at once (the emitter stops there).

emitRate.description: Particles the emitter adds per second (0: no emitter).

emitOffset.description: Where the emitter is, from the entity (world axes).

emitVelocity.description: The velocity emitted particles start with.

emitRadius.description: The half-size of the cube new particles appear in around the emitter.

sinkOffset.description: The sink's centre, from the entity (world axes).

sinkSize.description: The sink box: particles that enter it are removed (0 0 0: no sink).

color.description: The fluid's linear colour (what light passing through it keeps).

opacity.description: How opaque a metre of it is (0: clear as glass, 1: opaque).

reflectivity.description: How much it reflects (scales the Fresnel term).

refraction.description: How far refraction bends what is seen through it.

drawScale.description: The drawn size of each particle (times radius).

smoothing.description: How much the surface is smoothed (0: beads, 1: one surface).

WaterSurface.description: Height-field water (3D): a `resolution` × `resolution` grid of heights over a `size` square centred on the entity (its y is the rest level), waves travelling at `waveSpeed` and fading by `damping`. Dynamic bodies crossing it push waves (splashes; og.Splash events) and float by `buoyancy`. The heights are world state; an og.Water on the same entity draws them.

size.description: The side of the square of water.

damping.description: How much of a wave survives a second (1: no loss).

buoyancy.description: The upward force on a submerged body per cubic metre of its box under water (0: bodies sink).

drag.description: How much a submerged body's velocity is slowed.

WaterLine.description: 2D water for side-scrollers: a `width` × `depth` pool whose top edge (at the entity's y, centred on its x) is `columns` springs, each pulled to its rest height by `tension`, damped by `damping` and passing waves to its neighbours by `spread`. Bodies (and characters) crossing the surface splash it (og.Splash events) and float by `buoyancy`. The springs are world state; an og.Water2D on the same entity draws it.

depth.description: The pool's depth below the surface.

tension.description: How hard each spring pulls back to rest.

damping.description: How fast a spring's motion dies.

spread.description: How much of a spring's height its neighbours feel each pass (waves travel).

buoyancy.description: The upward force on a submerged body per square metre of its box under water (0: bodies sink).

drag.description: How much a submerged body's velocity is slowed.

Splash.description: Something crossed a water surface (og.WaterSurface or og.WaterLine): for splash particles and sounds. Read the next tick.

Ragdoll.description: A ragdoll over an og.Skeleton: a capsule body per bone with a parent, joints with limits between them (ball joints with cone limits in 3D; in 2D hinges about z, the bones rapier2d bodies in the xy plane at their animated z, for a skeleton laid out in that plane), built from the skeleton's rest pose. `weight` is where the pose comes from: 0 the animation (the bodies follow it kinematically), 1 the physics (the bodies are dynamic, starting with the animation's velocity); the pose drawn blends between them over `blendTime`, both ways. The bodies are world state (the og.physics state block), not entities.

weight.description: 0 animated, 1 ragdoll. Set it to 1 on a hit; back to 0 to recover.

blendTime.description: How long the blend between animation and physics takes, both ways.

mass.description: The whole body's mass, shared by the bones by length.

thickness.description: A bone capsule's radius as a fraction of its length.

jointLimit.description: How far each joint bends from the rest pose.

damping.description: How much of their motion the bones lose per second.

impulse.description: An impulse given to every bone when weight first goes up (a hit).

blend.description: Written: the blend in use (0 animation .. 1 physics).

QueryFilter.description: Which colliders a scene query considers. The zero value considers every solid collider on every layer.

mask.description: Layers to consider: a collider counts when its layers meet this; 0 means every layer.

exclude.description: An entity to ignore, such as the caster itself.

direction.description: Where it points; it need not be normalised and must not be zero (in 2D, not zero in xy).

maxDistance.description: How far it reaches; 0 is unbounded.

RaycastHit.description: The nearest collider a ray meets.

distance.description: From the origin along the normalised direction.

point.description: Where the ray meets the collider.

normal.description: The surface normal there (z is 0 in 2D).

ShapeDesc.description: The shape of a shape cast or an overlap test: the shape fields of a Collider. The zero value is a 1 m box.

radius.description: Radius of a sphere, circle, capsule or cylinder.

height.description: Capsule or cylinder height.

mesh.description: The geometry of a convex or triangle-mesh shape.

ShapeCastDesc.description: A shape swept along a direction for og.physics.shapeCast.

rotation.description: The shape's rotation; a zero quaternion is no rotation.

direction.description: Where it sweeps; it need not be normalised and must not be zero.

maxDistance.description: How far it sweeps; 0 is unbounded.

ShapeCastHit.description: The first collider a swept shape meets.

distance.description: How far the shape travelled before touching.

point.description: The contact point on the hit collider, in world space.

normal.description: The hit collider's surface normal there, in world space.

OverlapDesc.description: A shape placed in the world for og.physics.overlap.

rotation.description: Its rotation; a zero quaternion is no rotation.

MeshDesc.description: Geometry for convex and triangle-mesh colliders, in the mesh's own space.

positions.description: Vertex positions (2D polygons use x and y).

indices.description: Triangles as triples of indices into positions; a convex hull ignores them.

WheelPose.description: A wheel of an og.Vehicle as the last step left it, for drawing.

position.description: The wheel's centre in world space.

rotation.description: Its rotation (steering and spin) in world space.

RagdollBoneDesc.description: One bone of a ragdoll rig: a capsule from the bone's position along `axis` for `length`.

parent.description: The parent bone's index (it must come earlier); -1 for the root.

position.description: The bone's rest position relative to the entity.

rotation.description: The bone's rest rotation relative to the entity; a zero quaternion is no rotation.

length.description: How long the bone is (to its child).

axis.description: The direction the bone points in its own frame (towards its child).

joint.description: The skeleton joint (its index in the skin) the bone stands for, so the model is drawn with it; -1 for none.

RagdollRigDesc.description: The bones of a ragdoll, parents first, for og.physics.setRagdollRig; og.physics.ragdollRigFromSkeleton makes one from a model's skeleton.

skeleton.description: The skeleton the bones' joints belong to (0: none): the entity's posed model is drawn blended towards the bones by og.Ragdoll.blend.

BonePose.description: A ragdoll bone's pose as the last step left it (blended with the animation by og.Ragdoll.weight).

position.description: The bone's position in world space.

Fog.description: Distance and height fog over the 3D scene and world sprites: distance fog thickens exponentially by density from start (or linearly from start to end when end > start), height fog is densest below height and thins by falloff per metre above it; looking into the sun it turns towards sunColor. The overlay is never fogged.

color.description: The colour the fog tends to (linear, before exposure).

end.description: With end > start, a linear ramp to full fog at end as well.

heightDensity.description: Height fog at and below height (0: none).

height.description: The world height below which height fog is densest.

falloff.description: How fast height fog thins above height, per metre.

sunColor.description: The fog's colour looking into the sun (forward scattering).

sunPower.description: How tight the sun's glow in the fog is (higher: smaller).

sky.description: How much of the fog covers the sky (0: the sky stays clear).

Sky.description: A procedural sky of chosen colours, drawn behind the scene per pixel and lighting it (the image-based light follows it). Without it, RenderSettings.sky draws the built-in sky. A DayNight that is enabled sets the sky itself.

enabled.description: Draw and light by this sky.

sunSize.description: The sun disc's angular radius (0: no disc).

stars.description: Stars where the sky is dark: 0 none, 1 a full night sky.

brightness.description: A multiplier on the whole sky.

moonSize.description: The moon disc's angular radius (0: no moon). It sets below the horizon and hides the stars behind it.

moonPhase.description: How much of the moon is lit: 0 new, 0.25 the first quarter (its right half), 0.5 full, 0.75 the last quarter (its left half).

moonDirection.description: Towards the moon; zero puts it opposite sunDirection.

DayNight.description: A day-night cycle: the time of day drives the sun's direction, the sky's colours, stars and the moon disc, the first DirectionalLight (the sun by day, a dim moon opposite it by night), the ambient light and the fog's colour. The clock is start plus the simulated seconds times speed, wrapped to 24 hours; the image-based light is regenerated every `step` minutes of game time while the sky drawn per pixel moves smoothly.

start.description: The time of day at tick 0, in hours (6 sunrise, 12 noon, 18 sunset).

speed.description: Game hours per simulated second (0.05: a day in 8 minutes; 0 holds the time).

tilt.description: How far the sun's path leans from overhead.

azimuth.description: Where the sun rises, turned about +y from +x.

lightIntensity.description: A multiplier on the sun and moon light.

tintFog.description: Turn the og.Fog colour towards the horizon's.

step.description: Game minutes between regenerations of the image-based light.

moonSize.description: The moon disc's angular radius, opposite the sun so it rises as the sun sets (0: no moon).

moonPhase.description: How much of the moon is lit: 0 new, 0.25 the first quarter, 0.5 full, 0.75 the last quarter.

Weather.description: A weather preset around the camera: particles (rain, snow, dust), its fog (unless og.Fog is enabled, which takes precedence) and dimmed sunlight. Particles are simulated by the renderer from the tick, so they look the same on every run; they never touch the simulation.

intensity.description: How heavy: scales the particle rate, the fog and the dimming.

wind.description: Where the wind blows the particles.

radius.description: The size of the region around the camera the particles fill.

dim.description: How much of the preset's dimming of the sunlight applies.

layer.description: With an orthographic camera (2D), the sprite layer the particles draw in.

Water.description: A planar water surface on the entity's xz plane (centred on it, turned with it): colour by the water's depth over what is below, foam where it meets geometry, animated waves, refraction and reflections (screen-space where the tier allows, the sky's cubemap on WebGL2, or a planar reflection), the sun's shadows, caustics below it and an underwater view. With an og.WaterSurface on the same entity its wave heights displace the surface (centred on the entity, unrotated).

size.description: The extent along the entity's x and z.

segments.description: Grid cells per side (the height field's detail).

shallow.description: Shallow water's colour (tints what is seen through it).

depthFade.description: The depth over which water turns from shallow to deep.

foamWidth.description: The water depth over which foam rings geometry (0: none).

waveSpeed.description: How fast the detail waves travel.

waveStrength.description: How strongly they bend the surface (0: a mirror).

refraction.description: How far refraction shifts what is seen through the water.

planarReflection.description: Reflect the scene by drawing it again from the camera mirrored in the surface, at this fraction of the screen's resolution (0: off, the screen-space and sky reflections). One surface a frame, the first that asks; it costs about a second scene pass at that resolution.

shadows.description: How much the sun's shadows darken the surface: its highlight, foam and colour (0: none).

underwaterColor.description: With the camera below the surface: the water's fog colour.

underwaterDensity.description: Its fog per metre (0: no underwater view). Below the surface the frame's fog becomes the water's, and the surface seen from below shows the sky inside Snell's window.

caustics.description: Caustics of the sunlight on everything below the surface (0: none). One surface a frame, the first that has them.

Water2D.description: Draws the og.WaterLine on the same entity in the sprite order: the body from its surface down, a gradient from the top colour to the bottom one, and a bright lip along the surface.

top.description: The body's colour at the surface.

lipWidth.description: How thick the lip is (0: none).

layer.description: The sprite layer it is drawn in.

SkeletonAsset.description: A rig: a glTF's nodes in topological order with their rest transforms, and its skins (joints and inverse bind matrices).

ClipAsset.description: An animation clip, resampled at the cook's rate, with its markers.

GraphAsset.description: A blend-tree graph (`type animgraph`) whose clip references were resolved to clip handles.

RootMotion.description: What the root joint's motion does to the entity.

x-og-variants.off: The root animates in place; the entity does not move.
x-og-variants.planar: The root's horizontal (xz) travel and yaw move og.Transform.
x-og-variants.full: The root's whole translation and rotation move og.Transform.

x-og-variants.clips: The playing clips' weight channels write them.

IkSolver.description: How an IK chain is solved.

x-og-variants.twoBone: Analytic two-bone (thigh, shin, foot), bending towards the pole.

IkSpace.description: What an IK chain's target and pole are relative to.

x-og-variants.world: World positions: the skeleton entity's og.Transform applies.

Skeleton.description: A posed skeleton: the entity is drawn skinned by the joint palette og.anim writes each tick. The pose itself (every node's local transform) is world state kept by the `og.anim` state block.

skin.description: Which of the asset's skins the joint palette is for (glTF skin index).

rootMotion.description: Root motion extraction: off (animate in place), planar (xz travel and yaw move og.Transform) or full.

rootJoint.description: The joint whose motion is extracted (an index into the skin's joints; 0 is its first joint, usually the hips).

jointCount.description: Written: the number of joints in the palette (0 until the first tick).

AnimationPlayer.description: Plays one clip on a skeleton. Alone it poses the skeleton from its rest pose; with an og.AnimationGraph it plays over the graph's result with `weight`. Changing `clip` cross-fades from the previous one over `fade`; a clip change starts the new clip at 0 (or at `time` if the game wrote it in the same tick).

time.description: The playback position; written every tick, set it to seek (no markers fire across a seek).

speed.description: Playback rate (1 = as authored, negative plays backwards).

loop.description: Wrap at the end of the clip; otherwise hold the last frame and set `finished`.

weight.description: How much of the pose this player decides (0 = none, 1 = all).

finished.description: Written: a non-looping clip reached its end.

AnimationGraph.description: Runs a blend-tree graph (og.anim.graph) on a skeleton: its layers' state machines pick motions by the parameters p0...p7, which the graph names in `param` order (`param speed` is p0, the next `param` is p1, ...).

weight.description: How much of the pose the graph decides over the rest pose.

speed.description: A playback-rate multiplier for every layer.

state.description: Written: the base layer's current state (its index in the graph file).

stateTime.description: Written: seconds since the base layer entered `state`.

Blendshapes.description: Morph-target weights of the skeleton entity's mesh, in the order of the glTF mesh's targets. With `source` clips the playing clips' weight channels write them; with `component` game code does.

source.description: Who decides the weights: component (game code writes w0...w7) or clips (the animation writes them).

mesh.description: The glTF mesh index whose targets the weights drive (0 is the first mesh).

IkChain.description: An inverse-kinematics constraint on a skeleton, applied after its clips and graph: the chain of `bones` bones ending at joint `tip` turns so the tip reaches `target`. Put it on its own entity (a skeleton can have many chains); chains apply in query order.

skeleton.description: The entity with the og.Skeleton this chain bends.

tip.description: The end joint (an index into the skin's joints): the foot or the hand.

bones.description: How many bones above the tip turn (two-bone always uses 2).

solver.description: twoBone (analytic, with a pole) or fabrik (iterative, any length).

pole.description: A point the middle joint bends towards (two-bone); the zero vector keeps the animated bend.

space.description: What `target` and `pole` are relative to: world (the skeleton entity's og.Transform applies) or model.

weight.description: How much of the solved rotation is applied (0 = the animated pose, 1 = fully solved).

tolerance.description: The tip distance (model units) at which the target counts as reached.

reached.description: Written: the tip is within `tolerance` of the target after solving.

error.description: Written: the tip's distance from the target after solving, in model units.

AnimationEvent.description: A named marker of a clip that playback passed in the last tick (read in the tick after it fired, like every event). Cross-fades and blends fire every contributing clip's markers.

clip.description: The clip asset the marker belongs to.

time.description: The marker's time in the clip.

weight.description: The clip's blend weight when it fired.

ClipInfo.description: One clip of a loaded animation.

markers.description: Its markers' names, in time order.

Animation.description: What og.load.animation registered from a model's `#anim` blob.

nodes.description: The rig's node names, in topological order.

skins.description: Each skin's joint count, in glTF order.

morphTargets.description: Morph targets across the model's meshes.

text.description: The graph's `.ogt` text (`type animgraph`, `version 1`; the grammar is og-anim's README).

clips.description: The clips a `clip <motion> "<name>"` line may name, by ClipInfo.name: usually og.load.animation's `clips`.

Rig.description: A humanoid map from og.load.rig (a cooked `.ogt` of `type rig`): the naming scheme a skeleton's node names follow and the standard bones it names outright.

HumanBone.description: One standard humanoid bone of a skeleton.

bone.description: The standard bone: hips, spine, chest, upperChest, neck, head, then leftShoulder, leftUpperArm, leftLowerArm, leftHand, the right arm, leftUpperLeg, leftLowerLeg, leftFoot, leftToes and the right leg.

node.description: The skeleton node that is that bone.

Humanoid.description: Which node of a skeleton is each standard humanoid bone (what retargeting maps).

scheme.description: The naming scheme the bones were read in: mixamo, vrm, unity, rigify, ue or blender; custom when a rig named them, none when nothing matched.

bones.description: The bones found, in the standard order (hips first).

HumanoidDesc.description: A skeleton and, optionally, the rig that says how its bones are named.

rig.description: A humanoid map from og.load.rig; 0 detects the bones from the node names (Mixamo, VRM, Unity, Rigify, Unreal or Blender names).

RetargetDesc.description: A clip made for one skeleton, to play on another (other proportions, rest pose or bone names).

source.description: The skeleton the clip was made for (og.load.animation's `skeleton`: a character's, or an animation library's).

target.description: The skeleton that will play it.

sourceRig.description: How the source's bones are named (og.load.rig); 0 detects them.

targetRig.description: How the target's bones are named; 0 detects them.

footIk.description: Solve the legs so a planted foot stays planted on the target's ground (and the hips lower when a leg cannot reach).

FlipbookSheet.description: A sprite sheet's frames and clips (a cooked `.ogt` of `type flipbook`), from og.load.flipbook.

FlipMode.description: How a flipbook clip runs past its last frame.

x-og-variants.pingPong: Back and forth, without repeating the end frames.
x-og-variants.once: Hold the last frame and set Flipbook.finished.

Flipbook.description:
Plays a clip of a flipbook sheet on the entity's og.Sprite: extraction draws the sprite with the sheet's texture and the current frame's region and pivot (the sprite keeps its size, colour, flips and layer). Played by the engine's og.flipbook system by scaled time (Time.scaledDt: slow motion, hit stop), after the game's systems.
