Changing clip restarts at the clip's first frame (or at `time`, written in the same tick); writing a different time is a seek. Frame events are og.FlipbookEvent. The playback position is world state (the og.flipbook state block).

clip.description: The clip: an index into FlipbookInfo.clips (og.anim.clip finds one by name).

speed.description: The playback rate: 1 as authored, 2 twice as fast, 0 holds the frame.

frame.description: Written: the clip frame shown (an index into the clip's frames).

time.description: Seconds into the current cycle; written every tick, set it to seek (no events fire across a seek).

finished.description: Written: a `once` clip reached and holds its last frame.

loops.description: Written: cycles completed by a looping or ping-pong clip.

FlipbookEvent.description: A flipbook entered a frame its clip names in an `event` line (`event 2 "step"`): footsteps, the frame a hit lands, a pickup's sparkle. Read in the tick after, like every event; a clip started at 0 fires its first frame's events.

FlipbookClipInfo.description: One clip of a loaded flipbook sheet.

duration.description: Seconds of one cycle (a ping-pong cycle goes there and back).

mode.description: How it runs past its end.

events.description: Its events' names, in frame order.

texture.description: The sheet's texture (loaded with it; sampled nearest unless the sheet says `filter linear`).

frameWidth.description: The first frame's width in pixels.

frameHeight.description: The first frame's height in pixels.

Ease.description: An easing curve from the start (0) to the end (1). In starts slow, out ends slow, inOut both. back overshoots, elastic rings, bounce bounces at the end.

x-og-variants.quadOut: Gentle ease out: the default for most motion.
x-og-variants.linear: Constant speed: scrolling, timers, colour cycles.
x-og-variants.cubicOut: Ease out: UI sliding in, things settling.
x-og-variants.cubicInOut: In and out: camera moves, deliberate motion.
x-og-variants.expoIn: Exponential ease in: things falling away, warp-outs.
x-og-variants.backIn: Pulls back first, then goes: anticipation.
x-og-variants.backOut: Overshoots, then settles: pops, squash recovery, buttons.
x-og-variants.elasticOut: Rings after arriving: springy, cartoon impacts.
x-og-variants.bounceOut: Bounces at the end: drops, landings.

entity.description: The entity whose component is tweened.

component.description: The component token (og.Transform, og.Sprite, a game's own); null is og.Transform.

field.description: The field, or one lane of it: `position`, `position.y`, `scale`, `color.r`, `opacity`. f32, f64, i32 and u32 fields (rounded), vectors, colours and quaternions (as a rotation) tween; bool, enum and handle fields do not.

to.description: The end value: one number for a scalar or for every lane, or one per lane.

from.description: The start value, written from the tick the tween is started and held through its delay; null takes the field's value when the tween starts (after its delay).

relative.description: `to` is added to the start value.

duration.description: Seconds from start to end (one cycle).

loops.description: Extra cycles: 0 plays once, n repeats n more times, -1 forever.

yoyo.description: Every other cycle plays backwards (pulses, bobbing).

unscaled.description: Advance by real ticks, ignoring Time.scale and hit stop (UI motion).

tag.description: A number of yours, carried by og.TweenCompleted.

TweenGroupDesc.description: How a sequence or parallel group runs.

loops.description: Extra runs of the whole group: 0 once, -1 forever; each run replays the spans its tweens resolved in the first.

unscaled.description: Advance by real ticks, ignoring Time.scale and hit stop.

tag.description: A number of yours, carried by og.TweenCompleted.

TweenCompleted.description: A tween or group ended on its own (read in the tick after).

tween.description: The handle og.tween.to, sequence, parallel, squash or flash answered.

SquashDesc.description: Squash and stretch: the entity's og.Transform.scale jumps to rest times impact and eases back to rest.

impact.description: The x and y factors at the impact: (1.25, 0.8) squashes (a landing, a hit), (0.8, 1.25) stretches (a jump).

ease.description: The recovery curve; backOut overshoots a little, elasticOut wobbles.

FlashDesc.description: A hit flash: the entity's og.Sprite (else og.Mesh) flashColor set and its flash faded from amount to 0.

color.description: The flash colour (white for a hit, red for damage taken).

amount.description: How far it starts towards the colour.

ease.description: The fade's curve; quadIn holds the flash, then drops it.

TilemapAsset.description: A loaded map: its layers, tilesets and objects.

Tilemap.description: Draws a loaded map with its top-left corner at the entity's position (z included) and gives its collision layers static colliders. The og.tilemap system adopts it in the first tick it exists: from then on og.tilemap.setTile and getTile reach it.

layer.description: The sprite layer of the map's layer 0; every layer draws at this plus its z (default: its index).

collision.description: Give the layers marked collision static colliders (rectangles merged from the solid tiles).

colliderLayers.description: The collision layers of those colliders, as bits (Collider.layers).

index.description: Its index (what drawing order and z start from).

parallax.description: Its scroll factors: 1 1 moves with the world, 0.5 at half the camera's speed (far away), 0 stays with the camera.

terrain.description: The auto-tiling terrain of a terrain layer (its cells are 1 filled or 0 empty); empty for a tile layer.

TileObject.description: An object of a map (a Tiled object, an LDtk entity, an `object` block): spawn points, doors, triggers.

position.description: Its top-left corner, in world units relative to the map's top-left corner (y up, so below the corner is negative).

size.description: Its width and height (0 0 for a point).

center.description: Its centre, relative to the map's corner.

height.description: Cells down.

tileWidth.description: A cell's width in world units.

tileHeight.description: A cell's height in world units.

tile.description: A tile layer: the tile id, -1 empty. A terrain layer: 1 fills, 0 clears, and the neighbours re-tile.

inside.description: Whether the point was on the map.

AudioBus.description: The bus a source plays on; every bus passes through master.

x-og-variants.master: The master bus: what every bus passes through.

AudioSource.description:
A sound an entity plays. Level-triggered: while `playing` is true it plays (inserting a source plays it), setting it false stops it, and a one-shot that reaches its end sets it back to false and sends og.SoundEnded.
A one-shot of F frames at rate R and pitch p started in tick S ends in tick S + ceil(F * tickRate / (R * p)) - 1. A despawned entity's voice is silenced without an event.

sound.description: The sound, from og.load.sound; 0 plays nothing. A handle not yet loaded waits and starts on the first tick it is there.

pitch.description: Playback rate: 2 is an octave up and half as long.

pan.description: Stereo position of a non-spatial source, -1 left to 1 right.

loop.description: Loop between loopStart and loopEnd, seamlessly.

loopEnd.description: Where a loop wraps; 0 is the sound's end.

spatial.description: Attenuate and pan by the entity's og.Transform relative to the listener.

refDistance.description: Full volume up to this distance, as Web Audio's PannerNode.refDistance.

maxDistance.description: No quieter past this distance, as Web Audio's PannerNode.maxDistance.

rolloffFactor.description: How fast volume falls with distance, in Web Audio's inverse model: ref / (ref + rolloff * (clamp(d, ref, max) - ref)).

playing.description: Plays while true; the engine sets it false when a one-shot ends.

priority.description: When more than Audio.maxVoices would play, the lowest priority is stopped first (then the quietest, then the oldest), with SoundEnded reason SOUND_CULLED.

lowpass.description: A low-pass filter on this source, its cutoff; 0 is off.

occlude.description: A spatial source behind a collider (a physics ray to the listener) plays at Audio.occlusionGain through a low-pass at Audio.occlusionCutoff.

distanceCutoff.description: A spatial source's low-pass by distance: the cutoff at maxDistance, from 20 kHz at refDistance (log-linear between); 0 is off.

startAt.description: Starts at this world time (seconds since tick 0), to the sample, even inside a tick; 0 or a time past starts at once. Music.nextBar and Music.nextBeat give musical times.

startOffset.description: Where in the sound it starts, in seconds of the sound: started at startAt (or at once) from this far in, to the sample and at full gain, so a resumed phrase continues instead of restarting. Past a one-shot's end it plays nothing; a loop wraps into its region.

fade.description: Starts, stops and volume changes ramp over this long: a crossfade is one source stopped and another started with the same fade; 0 is 5 ms.

AudioListener.description: Where spatial sources are heard from: the entity's og.Transform, looking down its -Z with +X to the right. The first listener in query order is used.

volume.description: A gain on every spatial source this listener hears.

Audio.description: Bus volumes; master scales every bus. A change ramps over 256 frames in the mixer.

master.description: Gain of the master bus, applied to every sound.

maxVoices.description: The most sources that play at once; past it the lowest AudioSource.priority is stopped (SoundEnded reason SOUND_CULLED).

occlusionGain.description: The gain of an occluded source (AudioSource.occlude).

occlusionCutoff.description: The low-pass cutoff of an occluded source.

reverbRoom.description: The shared reverb's room size (the AudioBusFx.reverb sends feed it).

reverbDamping.description: The shared reverb's damping of high frequencies.

outputLatency.description: Seconds from a sample's world time to the speaker, as the host reports it (og.audio.outputLatency).

AudioBusFx.description:
A bus's insert effects: a high- and low-pass (12 dB/octave), a compressor, side-chain ducking by another bus, and a send to the shared reverb, whose return joins master. One entity per bus (the first in query order counts); without one a bus passes straight through.
Changes reach the mixer through the command stream, so they are deterministic and in the world hash; the PCM is the mixer's.

bus.description: The bus these effects are on.

reverb.description: How much of the bus goes to the reverb.

threshold.description: The compressor's threshold; 0 dB is off.

ratio.description: The compressor's ratio: dB in over the threshold per dB out.

duck.description: Turns this bus down while duckBus is loud: music under effects or dialogue.

duckBus.description: The bus that ducks this one.

duckDepth.description: How far it is turned down.

duckThreshold.description: How loud the key bus must be.

Music.description: A musical clock: tempo, metre and where bar 1 starts. The og.music system (before og.audio) writes the bar and beat and the times of the next beat and bar line every tick, and sends MusicBeat for every beat; an AudioSource whose startAt is nextBar starts on the bar line to the sample, so stems started together stay in step and a stinger lands on the downbeat.

start.description: The world time of bar 1's first beat.

bar.description: The bar the next tick starts in, from 1 (0 before start; written by og.music).

beat.description: The beat in that bar, from 1 (written by og.music).

nextBeat.description: The world time of the next beat from the next tick on (written by og.music).

nextBar.description: The world time of the next bar line from the next tick on (written by og.music).

MusicBeat.description: A beat of a Music clock, sent in the tick whose interval holds it (systems read it the tick after).

beat.description: The beat in the bar, from 1 (1 is the bar line).

SoundStarted.description: A source started, sent in the tick it happens (systems read it the tick after).

voice.description: The voice id in the command stream.

SoundEnded.description: A sound ended, sent in the tick it happens (systems read it the tick after).

voice.description: The voice id in the command stream.

reason.description: Why: SOUND_FINISHED (0), SOUND_STOPPED (1), SOUND_REMOVED (2), SOUND_REPLACED (3) or SOUND_CULLED (4).

Navigation.description: A grid, a navmesh or a flow field agents plan on.

NavAlgorithm.description: The grid search a path query runs.

x-og-variants.jps: Jump point search: the same optimal paths as A* with fewer nodes; on a grid with weighted cells it runs A*.

NavAgent.description: An entity that moves itself towards `target` while `seeking`, by a path over `nav` (a grid, navmesh or flow field; 0 goes straight). og.nav re-plans when the target moved more than repathDistance, every repathTicks, or when the grid or navmesh changed, at most 32 plans a tick across agents.

nav.description: The grid, navmesh or flow field it plans on (og.nav.grid, og.nav.load, og.nav.flowField); 0 moves straight at the target.

seeking.description: Moves towards the target while true.

radius.description: Its radius: grid paths keep this clear of walls; separation uses it.

stopDistance.description: It has arrived within this distance of the target.

slowRadius.description: It slows down inside this distance of the target.

repathTicks.description: Re-plans this often while seeking (0: only when the target moves).

repathDistance.description: Re-plans when the target moved farther than this from the last plan.

smooth.description: Pulls grid paths straight where nothing is in the way.

faceMovement.description: Turns the entity to face where it moves (3D: about +Y, its +Z forward; 2D: about +Z, its +X forward).

turnSpeed.description: How fast it turns when facing its movement.

drive.description: Moves the entity (its og.Velocity, or its og.Transform) while true; false keeps planning but leaves the motion to the game (a knock-back, a stun).

status.description: NAV_IDLE, NAV_MOVING, NAV_ARRIVED, NAV_UNREACHABLE or NAV_PARTIAL (written by og.nav).

waypoint.description: The path corner it heads for (written by og.nav).

remaining.description: The path length left (written by og.nav).

plans.description: Paths planned so far (written by og.nav).

Steering.description: Steering behaviours an og.NavAgent adds to its path following, each by weight (0 is off): flee, wander, pursue, evade, separation from other agents and avoidance of colliders ahead (three physics rays).

seek.description: Weight of following the path to the target (seek, then arrive at the end).

fleeRadius.description: It flees (and evades) only inside this distance (0: always).

wanderDistance.description: How far ahead the wander circle is.

wanderJitter.description: How fast the wander point moves round the circle.

pursue.description: An entity to pursue (seek where it will be, from its NavAgent or og.Velocity); 0: none.

evade.description: An entity to evade (flee where it will be); 0: none.

separation.description: Weight of keeping apart from other agents.

separationRadius.description: Other agents closer than this push it away.

avoidDistance.description: How far ahead the avoidance rays reach.

avoidMask.description: Collision layers the avoidance rays hit (0: every layer).

NavGridDesc.description: A grid of square cells over the plane: cell (0, 0)'s lower corner at `origin`, rows running up.

height.description: Cells up.

origin.description: Where cell (0, 0)'s lower corner is (x, y in 2D; x, z in 3D).

costs.description: Row-major cell costs from row 0 (0 blocked, 1 normal, up to 255 to avoid); empty: every cell 1.

inside.description: Whether the point was on the grid.

smooth.description: Pull a grid path straight where nothing is in the way.

points.description: Its corners, start and end included.

expanded.description: Cells or polygons the search took off its open list.

FlowDesc.description: A flow field over a grid.

targets.description: Where agents go: each point's cell is a target.

blocked.description: Boxes standing on the floor (walls, crates).

agentRadius.description: Walls are kept this far away.

tileSize.description: Cells per tile side: an obstacle rebuilds the tiles it touches.

mesh.description: What NavAgent.nav and the queries take.

eyeHeight.description: Its eyes are this far above its position (+y).

occlude.description: Colliders hide what is behind them.

occluders.description: Collision layers that block sight (0: every layer).

hearing.description: How far it hears a sound of loudness 1 (a source's volume).

memory.description: How long a lost target stays its target.

team.description: Its team: it perceives og.Perceivable entities of other teams.

forward.description: Where it looks; zero: the way it last moved (before it moves, the way its Transform faces: +Z in 3D, +X in 2D).

target.description: What it sees or remembers seeing (written by og.ai).

sees.description: It sees the target now (written by og.ai).

lastSeen.description: Where it last saw the target (written by og.ai).

sinceSeen.description: Seconds since it last saw a target (written by og.ai; 1e6 before the first time).

heard.description: It heard something this tick (written by og.ai).

sinceHeard.description: Seconds since it last heard something (written by og.ai; 1e6 before the first time).

eyeHeight.description: Agents look at a point this far above its position (+y).

ok.description: Whether it succeeded; og.platform.result has the data or the error.

key.description: The key: 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.

score.description: The score, or a time in seconds for an ascending board.

order.description: How the board sorts, fixed by its first submission.

count.description: How many entries: the top `count`, or `count` around the player.

reason.description: Why, as the game names it: `level.completed`, `daily.streak` (1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`).

amount.description: How many points the game asks for; the platform decides what it grants.

model.description: The model or service, when known (at most 80 characters).

Terrain.description: Draws a loaded terrain placed by the entity's world transform (centred on its position, turned and scaled with it), with its layers (as cooked, or as og.terrain.setLayer left them), casting shadows unless told not to.

castShadows.description: Cast the directional and local lights' shadows (it always receives them).

lodSpacing.description: The finest clipmap level's spacing (0: the terrain file's, or the samples' spacing).

TerrainScatter.description: Scatters copies of a mesh (grass, flowers, stones) over a loaded terrain near the camera, where one of its layers shows: on a jittered grid fixed to the terrain, so each copy keeps its place, size and turn as the camera moves, every cell growing one with the probability of the layer's weight there (its control-map channel times its slope and altitude rules, over all the layers' weights). Copies keep their size and thin out (dithered) over the outer `fade` of `distance`. The renderer places them itself, a chunk of the grid at a time, once, and draws the chunks in range: copies cost about nothing per frame while the camera stays. They grow over the og.Terrain drawing the same data, placed as it is. Drawn only: no colliders, and the copies are not entities.

geometry.description: The mesh, its origin at its root.

layer.description: The terrain layer that places it, 0 to 3.

density.description: Copies per square metre where the layer's weight is 1.

distance.description: How far from the camera, along x and z, copies are placed.

fade.description: The outer part of `distance` over which copies thin out to nothing.

align.description: How far copies lean with the ground: 0 upright, 1 along its normal.

seed.description: Another seed places the copies elsewhere.

minHeight.description: The lowest point above its entity.

collision.description: Whether its terrain file asks for a collider (`collision`, default true).

normal.description: The surface normal, smoothed between samples as the renderer shades it.

slope.description: The normal's angle from straight up.

inside.description: Whether the point is over the terrain (outside, the nearest edge answers).

origin.description: Where the terrain stands: its og.Terrain entity's world position.
